items.title: India's first Zika vaccine nears human trials after CDSCO panel review
items.author: Sanket Koul
items.summary: An expert committee has recommended Phase I clinical trials for the vaccine developed by Indian Immunologicals and Australia's Griffith University, following a review of non-clinical studies ...
items.body: An expert committee of India's apex drug regulatory body, the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO), has recommended that government-affiliated drugmaker Indian Immunologicals Limited (IIL) be allowed to conduct Phase I clinical trials of the country's first vaccine for the Zika virus. The vaccine has been developed in partnership with Australia's Griffith University. Zika is a mosquito-borne infection primarily transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, with no vaccines currently available against the disease, according to UNICEF. The recommendation to proceed with trials was given to Human Biologicals Institute (HBI), the human health division of IIL, by the CDSCO's Subject Expert Committee (SEC) on vaccines, according to the panel's minutes of the meeting dated November 12, reviewed by Business Standard. The recommendation came nearly two months after HBI first submitted its Phase I clinical trial protocol to the panel in September this year. The protocol proposed a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled study to evaluate the safety, reactogenicity and immunogenicity of a recombinant live attenuated Zika vaccine (freeze-dried) in healthy adult volunteers aged 18 to 50 years. At its September meeting, the committee had noted that while the firm had completed acute-dose and repeat-dose toxicity studies, along with animal immunogenicity and challenge studies, it had not submitted the scientific rationale for selecting the dose for the Phase I study. The panel had also sought statistical justification for the proposed sample size, the 3:1 randomisation ratio and the selection of cohorts based on non-clinical study findings. It added that HBI had submitted only a summary of the non-clinical studies rather than the complete study reports. “In view of the above and after detailed deliberation, the committee recommended that the firm should submit the above information for further deliberation,” the SEC had stated at its September 23 meeting. At its November meeting, the SEC reconsidered the proposal after HBI submitted the scientific rationale for dose selection and complete non-clinical study reports covering single-dose and repeat-dose toxicity, including immunogenicity studies. The recommendation comes two years after IIL signed a memorandum of agreement (MoA) with the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) to develop India's first recombinant live attenuated Zika vaccine. Under the agreement, ICMR will bear the costs of Phase I clinical trials, including expenses related to trial conduct, investigations and monitoring. The trials will be conducted at ICMR network sites across India. The SEC's recommendation is a regulatory step towards initiating human trials. The commencement of the study will depend on subsequent regulatory permission and trial-related arrangements. While Zika infection is typically mild and often does not require specific treatment, it can have severe consequences for pregnant women, potentially causing microcephaly and other congenital abnormalities in infants. In some cases, Zika infection may also result in Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS), a neurological disorder. India has experienced sporadic, localised outbreaks of Zika virus since its first confirmed cases in 2016. No confirmed cases of Zika-associated microcephaly or GBS have been reported in the country to date.

EVERETT, Washington, Nov 15 : Three-time world champion Ilia Malinin claimed the Skate America title in Everett on Saturday, winning the event for a fourth time and delighting audiences with a choreo spin inspired by his mother.
It marked a successful start to a campaign in which Malinin is seeking to balance the technical difficulty he is known for with greater artistic expression.
The American finished with a total score of 284.31 points after topping the short program on Friday and placing second in the free skate, securing victory by 9.58 points over Italy's Daniel Grassl.
Grassl produced the strongest free skate of the event, climbing from fourth after the short program to finish with 274.73, while Israel's Tamir Kuperman completed the podium on with 248.55 in his senior Grand Prix debut.

Performing his "Blue Eye Samurai" free skate, Malinin overcame a slightly awkward landing on his opening quad flip before nailing a triple Axel and quad toe loop.
The 21-year-old, nicknamed the "Quad God", then landed a quad Lutz-triple Axel-double Axel combination, adding a triple Lutz-double toe loop and a quad Salchow before bringing the crowd to its feet with his trademark backflip.
He opted against attempting his signature quadruple Axel, instead delighting the crowd with a choreo spin.
"It was definitely the most fun I've ever had, but skating that program, man, I'm tired," Malinin told NBC.
"My legs, at the end of the program, just nearly gave up on me, but I'm glad I was able to stay on my feet most of the time, and I'm just looking forward to how the program progresses in the future."
Malinin said his mother Tatiana Malinina, the 1999 Grand Prix Final champion, was a constant source of inspiration.
"She's been there for me ever since I was born, and I always appreciate everything she does for me," he said.
Malinin had a roller-coaster 2025-26 season. He saw his 14-event winning streak end at the Winter Olympics, where he finished eighth in the singles event, before rebounding weeks later to capture a third consecutive world title.
Malinin will return to action at the NHK Trophy in Japan in two weeks, where a podium finish is expected to secure his place at December's Grand Prix Final, an event he has won in each of the last three seasons.

Source: Reuters

FAST

NEW YORK, Nov 15 : American Kayla Harrison leveraged her tremendous grappling skills to snatch a fourth-round submission win over Amanda Nunes on Saturday night as she retained her UFC bantamweight title, thwarting her opponent's attempt to take the belt back after more than three years out of the cage. 
In the main event at UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden, Ciryl Gane of France defeated American Josh Hokit by unanimous decision to retain the heavyweight title after a bruising five-round battle fought at a frenetic pace. 
A two-time Olympic judo champion, the 36-year-old Harrison was facing arguably the greatest female fighter of all time in Nunes, a dominant two-weight champion at bantamweight and featherweight before she stepped away from the sport in June 2023. But the Brazilian could not shake off the rust of her long absence as she let the fight slip away from her. 
Nunes did well initially, looking crisp in her striking and avoiding some early takedown attempts, but she eventually succumbed to Harrison's grappling attack, spending much of the latter part of the opening two rounds on the bottom in a scarf-hold position from which she struggled to escape.

Emboldened by her success, Harrison displayed the full range of her judo skills with perfectly timed trips and tosses and vice-like ground control. In the fourth round, she chased Nunes down to the mat, jumping on her back and quickly sinking in a rear-naked choke that forced the 38-year-old to submit. 
“I think I’m still in shock,” said Harrison, who had surgery on herniated disks in her neck in January. 
“It feels surreal. Sometimes I can’t believe my life. I’m just really grateful, I’m humble, it’s an honour and a privilege to stand before you."

items.author: CNA

Bahrain issues first threat alerts since September as Iran says it attacked US base

Bahrain urges people to stay calm and head to the nearest safe location after issuing two threat alerts as Iran claims a US base attack.

Cars drive past a billboard that reads, "Bahrain is Safe ... Because you are its People" in Manama on Jun 25, 2026. (Photo: Eric Lee/Pool/AFP)

FAST

Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Sunday (Nov 15), its first such warnings since September, as Iran said it had attacked a US base in the Gulf country amid uncertainty over a US-Iran deal aimed at ending the nearly nine-month-old war.
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it had attacked a US military base in Bahrain in retaliation for "hostile US actions", Iran's Fars news agency reported.
The Revolutionary Guards said they had launched six drones targeting a US air-defence radar at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base in Bahrain, Iranian state-run Press TV reported. There was no immediate confirmation from US or Bahraini authorities.
Bahrain, home to the US Navy's Fifth Fleet, urged citizens and residents to remain calm and proceed to the nearest safe location, the interior ministry said. It did not provide further details on the threats.

Two days earlier the Revolutionary Guards said they had attacked a US early-warning radar in Bahrain . The US military denied this, saying it had intercepted two Iranian drones without any damage.
Diplomatic efforts to end the conflict have yet to produce a breakthrough, though Washington and Tehran have held off on direct attacks in the war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb 28 and then spread across the region, with Tehran launching missile and drone attacks on US bases in Gulf countries.
President Donald Trump has said in recent days that he might hold off on attacking Iran if the US faces no new provocations from Tehran or the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, but that he would maintain a US naval blockade, Reuters reported on Saturday.
On another front, however, the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition fighting them have continued to exchange attacks, with the coalition saying on Sunday it had intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles launched towards the Saudi capital Riyadh and three drones in the kingdom's oil-rich Eastern Province.

items.title: Bahrain issues first threat alerts since September as Iran says it attacked US base
items.author: The Straits Times
items.summary: Bahrain urged citizens and residents to remain calm and proceed to the nearest safe location.
items.body:
Bahrain issues first threat alerts since September as Iran says it attacked US base
Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox

A bazaar in downtown Manama, Bahrain. Bahrain has urged citizens and residents to remain calm and move to the nearest safe location.
PHOTO: REUTERS

Published   Nov 15, 2026, 01:24 PM

Updated   Nov 15, 2026, 02:12 PM

Set as preferred source

Listen

Bahrain issued two alerts of potential threats on Nov 15, its first such warnings since September, as Iran said it had attacked a US base in the Gulf country amid uncertainty over a US-Iran deal aimed at ending the nearly nine-month-old war.
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it had attacked a US military base in Bahrain in retaliation for “hostile US actions”, Iran’s Fars news agency reported.
The Revolutionary Guards said they had launched six drones targeting a US air-defence radar at the Al-Rifaa helicopter base in Bahrain, Iranian state-run Press TV reported.

There was no immediate confirmation from US or Bahraini authorities.
Bahrain, home to the US Navy’s Fifth Fleet, urged citizens and residents to remain calm and proceed to the nearest safe location, the interior ministry said. It did not give further details.
Two days earlier, the Revolutionary Guards said they had attacked a US early-warning radar in Bahrain. The US military denied this, saying it had intercepted two Iranian drones without any damage.

Diplomatic efforts to end the conflict have yet to produce a breakthrough, though Washington and Tehran have held off on direct attacks in the war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb 28 and then spread across the region, with Tehran launching missile and drone attacks on US bases in Gulf countries.
President Donald Trump has said in recent days that he might hold off on attacking Iran if the US faces no new provocations from Tehran or the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen, but that he would maintain a US naval blockade, Reuters reported on Nov 14.
On another front, however, the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition fighting them have continued to exchange attacks, with the coalition saying on Nov 15 it had intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles launched towards the Saudi capital Riyadh and three drones in the kingdom’s oil-rich Eastern Province. REUTERS

items.title: フィギュア＝世界王者マリニン優勝、山本は7位　スケートアメリカ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［１４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［１４日　ロイター］ - フィギュスケートのグランプリ（ＧＰ）シリーズ第４戦、スケートアメリカは１４日、米ワシントン州エバレットで競技を行い、男子では世界王者のイリア・マリニン（米国）が優勝した。

ショートプログラム（ＳＰ）首位のマリニンは、この日のフリーでは２位。冒頭の４回転フリップの着氷が乱れたが、合計２８４．３１点で自身の今季初戦を勝利で飾った。

ＳＰ４位のダニエル・グラッスル（イタリア）がフリーで１位となり、合計２７４．７３点で２位。タミール・クーパーマン（イスラエル）が合計２４８．５５点で３位に入った。

ＳＰ２位の山本草太はフリーでは１０位とふるわず、合計２３１．３４点で７位に終わった。

items.title: Del fútbol a la guerra, el estadio de Haití que Bukele destinará a operaciones militares
items.author: Carlos Cuevas
items.summary: El recinto deportivo, que no recibe a la selección haitiana desde 2021, será el centro de operaciones de los militares salvadoreños desplegados para avanzar sobre territorios controlados por las pandi ...
items.body: Bloomberg Línea — El principal escenario deportivo de Haití, el estadio Sylvio Cator, donde la selección nacional de fútbol no disputa un partido desde hace cinco años, se convertirá temporalmente en una base operativa de las Fuerzas Armadas de El Salvador, que participan en las operaciones para someter a las pandillas y reducir su control en algunos territorios del país. Ver más: ¿Quiénes son los presidentes con mejor y peor imagen de Latinoamérica? Del respaldo a Sheinbaum y Bukele al derrumbe de Kast El estadio tiene capacidad para aproximadamente 10.000 espectadores y acogió por última vez al seleccionado haitiano el 12 de junio de 2021, en la derrota 0-1 ante Canadá por las Eliminatorias de la Concacaf rumbo a la Copa Mundial Catar 2022. Poco más de tres semanas después de ese encuentro, el 7 de julio, el entonces presidente de Haití, Jovenel Moïse, fue asesinado en su residencia por un comando armado integrado por exmilitares colombianos y colaboradores haitianos. El magnicidio profundizó la crisis política e institucional del país, mientras las pandillas ampliaban su control territorial. El 90% de Puerto Príncipe llegó a estar bajo el yugo de los grupos armados ilegales, de acuerdo con la ONU, e infraestructuras clave como el aeropuerto Toussaint Louverture permanecieron cerradas durante meses en el contexto de una creciente ola de violencia. En ese contexto, la selección de Haití disputó sus partidos como “local” en escenarios de República Dominicana, Barbados, Puerto Rico y Jamaica. Y rumbo al Mundial 2026, edición a la que clasificó luego de 52 años, hizo de su sede Curazao. El estadio —que estuvo bajo la custodia de las pandillas— fue recuperado el pasado 12 de noviembre por la Policía Nacional, las Fuerzas Armadas de Haití, soldados salvadoreños desplegados por orden del presidente Nayib Bukele y la Task Force, integrada por mercenarios de la compañía de seguridad privada Vectus Global, de Erik Prince. Bukele, justamente, fue quien anunció la intervención militar para retomar el control del Sylvio Cator. Lo hizo a través de una publicación en X con un mensaje en criollo haitiano y un video. “Durante la operación, encontramos varios cráneos humanos dentro del estadio”, escribió el mandatario salvadoreño. “Ahora estableceremos una base operativa en el estadio para poder avanzar más adentro del territorio controlado por las bandas”. Esta fue la primera vez en que Bukele habló del mecanismo que permitió el despliegue de alrededor de 2.000 uniformados de El Salvador en Haití: se trató de un acuerdo bilateral, aunque no hay mayores detalles ni información de si las tropas responden a un mando unificado. La Policía Nacional de Haití confirmó lo dicho por Bukele en un comunicado que publicó en Facebook. “Tras la recuperación de la zona, la PNH hizo entrega del control a las Fuerzas Armadas de El Salvador, que tomaron el relevo para consolidar la seguridad en estos espacios”, dice el documento. Aunque el contingente de 2.000 soldados que el presidente de El Salvador, Nayib Bukele, no ha encontrado a sus cuatro connacionales desaparecidos desde el pasado 18 de octubre en Haití, recuperó el estadio y propinó un ataque contra el cuartel general de la pandilla 400 Mawozo, liderada por Lanmò San Jou , en cuestión de una semana. La banda 400 Mawozo permanece activa en el área metropolitana de Puerto Príncipe, especialmente en el municipio de Croix-des-Bouquets, y es aliada de la coalición de bandas G-Pep, de acuerdo con la ONU. San Jou, de 33 años, luce cicatrices considerables por todo el cuerpo. Además, tiene tatuajes, entre los que sobresalen una calavera, una serpiente, una telaraña y un cuchillo. El FBI de los Estados Unidos actualmente ofrece una recompensa de US$1 millón por información que conduzca a la captura de San Jou, quien padece problemas renales y, por sus vínculos de la República Dominicana, se cree que podría viajar allí. Bukele ha planteado que, así como sometió a las pandillas Mara Salvatrucha y Barrio 18 en El Salvador, puede hacerlo con las estructuras armadas haitianas. “Si acabamos con las pandillas de acá, podemos acabar con ellos”, sostuvo antes de las intervenciones en mención. Ver más: Salvadoreños secuestrados en Haití: ¿por qué encontrarlos será como “buscar una aguja en un pajar”?

items.title: Flight Ground Stop Leaves Travelers Scrambling for Ways Home
items.author: list.metadata.agency
items.summary: It was arguably one of the worst times for a nationwide flight grounding: Friday, late afternoon, just as people were heading to airports for weekend jaunts or to return home from business trips.
items.body: (Bloomberg) -- It was arguably one of the worst times for a nationwide flight grounding: Friday, late afternoon, just as people were heading to airports for weekend jaunts or to return home from business trips.The ground stop from the Federal Aviation Administration, called around 4 p.m. Eastern time Friday, left passengers across the country stranded on tarmacs and stuck in terminals awaiting news of when — or if — their flights would take off. At New York’s LaGuardia Airport Friday evening, there wasn’t a seat to be found in the United Airlines terminal and bars were packed as passengers waited for news. Lines snaked around customer service at Chicago O’Hare International Airport. At Dallas Love Field, the scene at one security checkpoint was a rarity heading into the weekend: completely barren. The FAA lifted the ground stop just over four hours after it began. But by then, travelers had spent hours watching flight boards with estimated times ticking up and weighing how long they would wait before giving up. For some, that meant a quick calculation whether to stick it out and hope flights would resume, or start racing fellow stranded travelers for hotel rooms, rental cars or other ways home.“I have no idea what’s happening,” said Bernadeta Serafin, a Brooklyn resident who was trying to get to Fort Lauderdale, Florida, from John F. Kennedy International Airport to see a Friday night show. “What can I do?”The nationwide ground stop — only the third in US history — came at the end of what had already been a remarkable week of tech-related events, from the downfall of Jensen Huang, one of the most powerful names in AI, to a widespread outage of Microsoft Corp. products including Outlook, Teams and Copilot. The flight shutdown stemmed from a communications outage tied to a data overload, said Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy.Duffy said Saturday that officials are looking into whether aerospace and defense contractor L3Harris Technologies Inc. was at fault for the shutdown. The company did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters just after the ground stop that there was no indication of a threat. Microsoft said there was no sign it was tied to any of its services. With few details of what was happening Friday, rumors and gossip filled the vacuum. “I’m a little bit nervous to fly because yesterday the emails were all down,” said Lauren Sklarin, who was at JFK awaiting a flight to West Palm Beach, Florida. She was eager to get to her new condo in Delray Beach — a furniture delivery was arriving Saturday.More than 4,500 flights within, into or out of the US had been canceled and about 4,600 delayed as of 1:22 p.m. New York time Saturday, according to FlightAware. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said airlines expect to resume normal flight schedules by the end of business Sunday.At O’Hare on Saturday morning, Ellen Rendle, a 64-year-old librarian, was back at the gate trying to get home to Delaware. She’d booked a hotel after spending three hours at the airport Friday as her flight was pushed back an hour at a time. The Uber to her hotel cost $100. “They know everybody’s desperate,” she said. Her rebooked flight appeared to be on time, but even if it left as scheduled, she’d miss a memorial service she’d hoped to attend.Some passengers in New York had to endure a second straight evening of travel tumult after stormy weather caused flight cancellations Thursday. Xander Blood was supposed to fly home to the San Diego area Thursday evening after a trip with friends. It took him until 2 a.m. to find a hotel — ending up in Floral Park, Queens. He didn’t know what he’d do if he’s stuck again.“This is the second day,” Blood said. “It’s a bummer.”Passengers already aboard planes faced a different sort of limbo. A Delta Air Lines Inc. flight bound for Richmond, Virginia, had been in line for takeoff at LaGuardia when the pilot told passengers of the communications issue and headed back toward the terminal. But with arriving planes occupying gates, there was nowhere to park, leaving passengers to sit on the plane for hours sharing snacks and making backup plans. Michelle Otey was on her way to Boston from California and about 20 minutes from landing when she got an alert on her phone about the FAA ground stop. The flight crew didn’t make an announcement acknowledging it, she said, leaving her to search online to figure out what was happening.“How are we landing a plane without air traffic control?” she wondered. “We’re just winging it?” The flight ultimately landed normally.In Chicago, Melissa Dzeletovic had taken her 15-year-old son, Luka, to O’Hare for his first flight by himself — a trip to visit a cousin in Atlanta. He boarded the plane and moments before they were set to take off he called his mom and told her there was an issue. Dzeletovic decided to take him back home and reschedule the trip.“He was on the plane for about 10 to 15 minutes, and then they asked them to get off the plane, and he’s been waiting by the gate for a couple of hours,” she said. “I’m going to take him because I’m already nervous that he’s in this situation.”Kirk Framke, an eighth grade math teacher from Denver, arrived at Los Angeles International Airport with a large group of students returning from a marine biology camp on Catalina Island. With their cell phones stashed in a chaperone’s bag, the students had no idea what was happening. “There are no flights taking off anywhere in the entire United States,” Framke told them, prompting groans and an audible “What?”Framke said school officials were making arrangements for a charter bus to make the 1,000-mile, 15-hour drive back to Denver, if they weren’t able to get a flight home Friday. In the meantime, the group planned to order pizzas to the check-in area and break out games such as Exploding Kittens and Taco Cat.--With assistance from Millie Munshi, Myles Miller, Julie Fine, Hani Shawwa and Anne Riley Moffat.(Updates with latest flight figures in 9th paragraph and traveler comments in 10th)More stories like this are available on bloomberg.com©2026 Bloomberg L.P.

items.title: AI retreat fuels India stock comeback in great rotation trade
items.author: Bloomberg
items.summary: Indian stocks are staging a strong comeback as global investors rotate away from crowded AI bets towards markets with improving earnings and attractive valuations. Falling oil prices and renewed foreign inflows are further supporting the recovery.
items.body: Indian stocks suffered bruising losses in the first nine months of the year as the artificial intelligence trade hoovered up global investor capital. The unwinding of that strategy has turned the Asian nation’s equities into world beaters.The MSCI India gauge has rebounded 11% from a six-month low set in October, adding more than $400 billion in value and almost erasing this year’s losses, as the country’s relative lack of AI exposure has become a prime advantage. Global funds are also turning more positive on India’s $5.4 trillion equity market as oil prices retreat and earnings growth accelerates.“We’ve become more positive on India and have added back to our exposure in recent weeks,” said Tan Altundag, an investment manager for emerging equities at Pictet Asset Management in Hong Kong. “We see an improving balance between macro headwinds, portfolio flows and valuations,” while “diversification away from the increasingly volatile AI trade also appears likely to benefit India,” he said.The bounceback in Indian shares over the past month illustrates a broader rotation by global funds away from crowded tech bets toward markets backed by strong earnings. The shift signals a potential turning point for emerging markets as a whole, testing whether the world’s fastest-growing major economy can reclaim its status as a premier alternative to US tech giants after months of trailing its global peers.135847076A return of overseas investors has underpinned the rebound in Indian stocks, and the process may still have room to run as global funds remain largely underweight.Overseas buyers have snapped up a net $8.5 billion of Indian shares in November, heading for the biggest monthly inflow in six years, according to data compiled by Bloomberg. That has reduced this year’s total outflow to about $22 billion.Active long-only funds globally remain $74 billion underweight on Indian shares relative to the benchmark, Bank of America data show, close to their lightest positioning since the bank began compiling the figures in 2015.Earnings for Nifty 50 Index companies may rise around 18% year-on-year in the September quarter, accelerating from 13% growth in the prior three months, Bank of America data also show.US-based Calamos Investments is among those boosting its holdings.The money manager’s emerging-market strategy has lifted its India allocation to more than 10% over the past three to four months from as little as 1% to 2% about a year ago, co-chief investment officer Nick Niziolek said.“We’re adding to India because we’re seeing an inflection in earnings,” he said. “We’re seeing an improvement in fundamentals, and we see really attractive valuations.”135847085Kabouter Management LLC is another overseas investor that is growing more positive.“As long-term investors, we remain constructive on the outlook for India,” said Nikhil Rastogi, portfolio manager at the Chicago-based money manager.Indian shares have faced many challenges in the past two years, “but these headwinds don’t change the long-term picture, and some of the global shifts behind them are working in India’s favor,” he said. “Valuations that looked stretched two years ago have become more attractive, particularly in pockets of the market.”The MSCI India gauge trades at a price-to-earnings ratio of about 20 times one-year-ahead profits, a discount to its five-year average, data compiled by Bloomberg show.The recent decline in oil prices is also helping shares in India, which imports nearly 90% of its energy needs.Global benchmark Brent crude has dropped over 18% from a high set on Oct. 30 as investors wager that the Democratic Party’s sweep of the US Congress in November’s midterm elections has increased the likelihood of an end to the Middle East conflict.“I’m comfortable on India while Brent sits around $100 a barrel or below,” said Lauren Hyslop, an investment manager at UK-based Mattioli Woods.Despite the recent rally in Indian stocks, the market remains a relative laggard for 2026. MSCI’s India gauge has still dropped 2.2% this year, whereas the index provider’s regional benchmark has jumped about 12%. The Indian measure is on track for back-to-back years of underperformance against its regional peer for the first time since 2020, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.Fidelity Investment Management is broadly positive on India, but it isn’t rushing back in.“We have reduced some underweight on India over the past few weeks by trimming some AI-related stocks,” said Nick Price, an emerging-market portfolio manager at Fidelity in Hong Kong. “There’s no rush and it remains underweight, but India exposure may rise in a slow and deliberate manner from my side,” especially through financial stocks, he said.Others are content to hold on to stocks that they see as offering value for the long term.“With the unwinding of AI trades, we’ve seen buying interest coming back for India,” said Simon Sidmalm, a fund manager at Tundra Fonder AB in Stockholm. “We’re holding on to the value names we see upside in from a fundamental perspective longer term.”

items.title: Mike Johnson Calls for 'Investment,' Not Probe, After FAA Ground Stop as Duffy's $50 Billion Ask Draws Fire From Greene
items.summary: House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) said Saturday that Congress doesn’t need to investigate Friday’s nationwide FAA ground stop, but it does need to fund upgrades."We don’t really need any ...
items.body:
News
/ Benzinga
/ Mike Johnson Calls for 'Investment,' Not Probe, After FAA Ground Stop as Duffy's $50 Billion Ask Draws Fire From Greene

Mike Johnson Calls for 'Investment,' Not Probe, After FAA Ground Stop as Duffy's $50 Billion Ask Draws Fire From Greene 2 min read

LHX
House Speaker Mike Johnson (R-La.) said Saturday that Congress doesn’t need to investigate Friday’s nationwide FAA ground stop, but it does need to fund upgrades.
"We don’t really need any investigation … we need further investment," Johnson said on Fox News’ "Saturday in America." He noted that some equipment dates to the 1980s.

Saturday in America
@SatAmericaFNC

🚨SPEAKER MIKE JOHNSON SAYS HOUSE IS WORKING ON FAA FUNDING AFTER NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP @SpeakerJohnson tells @KayleighMcEnany he’s in Washington this weekend working on legislation to modernize America’s air traffic control system.
"We’re going to work to get it done."⬇️… pic.twitter.com/V6Dms1cNqO

Nov 14, 2026

Router Fault Under Review
Government officials said Saturday a single router installed by L3Harris Technologies Inc. LHX may have caused the outage, Reuters reported. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the cause remains undetermined.
Duffy said Friday the contractor was switching lines from copper wire to fiber.
In a statement, L3Harris said it has completed more than 70% of that conversion and is supporting the FAA’s investigation.
Duffy said the new routers flooded others with over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds. The routers being replaced are about 25 years old, Duffy said, and were due for replacement in 2006.
Rare Stoppage Disrupts Air Travel
The FAA issued the ground stop around 4 p.m. EST Friday. Duffy said it was lifted around 8:15 p.m. The agency’s last widespread stoppage lasted about 90 minutes in January 2023 .
As of 9:25 p.m. EST Saturday, FlightAware data showed 8,048 delays and 6,445 cancellations within, into or out of the U.S.
$50 Billion Funding Push
On Friday, Duffy called the system "incredibly old" and said, "I want $50 billion." Congress has already given the FAA $12.5 billion for upgrades.
In a Saturday post on X, Duffy called modernization a " national safety priority ." He said Congress needs to step up with resources to build a "state-of-the-art system."
Greene And Torres Question Aviation Funding
Former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene (R-Ga.) criticized the $50 billion funding request .
In a long post on X on Saturday, she said she was "blown away" by people who "fell for the total garbage" at Friday’s press conference, and said officials lied about what happened.
She said the systems need updating and "it takes money," but that officials have "plenty of money."

Marjorie Taylor Greene 🇺🇸
@mtgreenee

I’m literally blown away by the amount of people that fell for the total garbage that they got fed at that press conference yesterday.
If you’re an American, we as a country are in over $40 trillion in debt, have spent approximately $15 trillion in foreign countries and foreign…

Nov 14, 2026

Rep. Norma Torres (D-Calif.) wrote on X, "Before asking taxpayers for more, this administration owes answers about how existing funds are being spent and why our aviation system is still falling behind."

Rep. Norma Torres
@NormaJTorres

Sean Duffy wants $50 billion to fix our air traffic control system. But Congress already provided $12.5 billion for FAA modernization, and DOT and OMB have requested another $30.1 billion.
Before asking taxpayers for more, this administration owes answers about how existing… https://t.co/eOOEvEpTE0

items.title: サッカー＝スペイン代表監督、「スペインに人種差別はない」
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［マドリード　１４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［マドリード　１４日　ロイター］ - サッカーの欧州ネーションズリーグ（ＮＬ）のイングランド戦を前に、スペイン代表のルイス・デラフエンテ監督が１４日、「スペインに人種差別はない」と明言した。

スペインとイングランドはリーグＡ３組の首位を懸けて１５日にマドリードで対戦。イングランドが同地で試合を行うのは２００４年の国際親善試合以来となる。その試合ではアシュリー・コールやショーン・ライトフィリップスなどの黒人選手が観客から人種差別的な野次を浴びていた。

スペインはことし３月にバルセロナで行われた国際親善試合でエジプトと対戦したが、その際にサポーターがイスラム教徒を標的とした差別的チャントを行い、国際サッカー連盟から罰金処分を命じられている。

対戦を前にイングランド代表ＭＦデクラン・ライスは、同様の問題が発生した場合、チームは決められたプロトコルに従って行動するとコメント。また「今回はそのようなことは起こらないと思う。素晴らしいスタジアムであり、私たちが非常に敬意を抱いている選手たちとの対戦だ。とてもいい夜になるはずだ」と記者団に話した。

これに先立ち、イングランド代表のトーマス・トゥヘル監督は、差別的な野次は起こらないだろうとしつつ、選手たちにはプロトコルを改めて周知するとしていた。

これに対し、デラフエンテ監督は報道陣に「私に言えるのは、スペインには人種差別などないということ。トーマスに伝えてほしい。私はそう強く感じている。イングランドと同じようにスペインにも人種差別はない」とコメント。一方のトゥヘル監督はこの発言を受け、「私はスペインの人種差別について話したことはない」とし、一部のメディアが自身の発言を歪曲して伝えていると不快感を示した。

items.title: ウクライナ大統領、米スペースＸの通信制限を批判　「防空網が弱体化、政治的意味合いも」
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［キーウ　１４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［キーウ　１４日　ロイター］ - ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は１４日、米スペースＸの軍事用衛星通信端末「スターシールド」の速度制限を巡り、重要な防空網を弱体化させ、政治的にも危険な意味を持つと批判した。ロシアによる一時占領地では過去５日間、スターシールド端末を搭載して時速１６１キロ以上で移動すると通信が制限される状態が続き、軍事作戦に支障が出ているという。

ゼレンスキー氏は、この制限によりウクライナの防空部隊がロシアの高速ドローンを迎撃することがより困難になり、国内の都市が脅威にさらされていると述べた。

同国の国防省はすでにスペースＸに対し、この問題を公式に提起しているもようだ。

同氏は１４日の会見で「制限が導入されてから５日が経過した。スペースＸは何らかの技術的な問題だと言っているが、われわれはそうは考えていない」と述べた。

さらに「もしそこで制限を課すなら、一時的に占領された地域をウクライナの領土ではないと部分的に認めていることになる。だからこそ、我々にはこの問題を提起し、速度制限を撤廃して、一切の制限がない状態に戻す権利があると考える」と語った。

スペースＸは、新たな制限を導入したり、衛星運用に変更を加えたことはないと否定している。

このような通信障害が発生したのは今回で２回目となる。

items.title: サッカー＝欧州ＮＬでスウェーデン昇格決める、ギェケレシュ8戦連続ゴール
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［１４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［１４日　ロイター］ - サッカーの欧州ネーションズリーグ（ＮＬ）は１４日、各地で１次リーグの試合を行い、リーグＢの４組ではスウェーデンがボスニア・ヘルツェゴビナに３─２で競り勝ち、１試合を残してリーグＡへの昇格を決めた。

スウェーデンは前半５分にダニエル・スベンソンのゴールで先制すると、同１１分にビクトル・ギェケレシュがＰＫを沈めて大会８試合連続ゴールをマーク。ギェケレシュはアディショナルタイムにもＰＫを決めて今大会６点目を挙げた。後半、ボスニアに２点を奪われるも、１点のリードを守り切った。

リーグＢ４組のもう１試合ではルーマニアがポーランドに２─１で勝利した。

この結果、同組ではスウェーデンが勝ち点１３で首位を確定し、次大会からリーグＡへの昇格が決まった。同８で２位のボスニアは昇格を懸けてプレーオフに臨む。

リーグＢの３組ではオーストリアがアイルランドに１─０で勝利。勝ち点１１で首位を確定し、リーグＡへの昇格を果たした。

items.title: フィギュア＝ＧＰ2連勝目指す中井が女子ＳＰ首位、スケートアメリカ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［１４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［１４日　ロイター］ - フィギュスケートのグランプリ（ＧＰ）シリーズ第４戦、スケートアメリカは１４日、米ワシントン州エバレットで競技を行い、女子ショートプログラム（ＳＰ）では中井亜美がトップだった。

第１戦のフランス大会に続くＧＰ２連勝を目指す中井は、冒頭のトリプルアクセル（３回転半ジャンプ）などのジャンプを着氷。スピンやステップなどもうまくまとめて、自己ベストの８２．２０点をマークした。

ロシアから個人の中立選手（ＡＩＮ）として出場しているアレクサンドラ・イグナトワが７４．２４点で２位、金有材（韓国）が７３．９２点で３位、松生理乃は７０．３０点で５位だった。

Israeli military says it struck senior member of Hamas military wing

FAST

JERUSALEM: The Israeli military said on Sunday (Nov 15) its forces had struck a senior militant from Hamas's military wing, which confirmed the death of one of its commanders in Gaza.
Samir Abu Younis, a military leader who played a key role in planning Hamas's Oct 7, 2023 attack on Israel, was killed on Saturday, according to a statement from the Islamist movement's Al-Qassam Brigade.
"A short while ago, the IDF and ISA struck a senior terrorist in Hamas' military wing," the Israeli military said in a joint statement with internal security agency Shin Bet, in the early hours of Sunday morning.
It did not elaborate but said it would later provide further details.
"He was killed yesterday evening ... in a cowardly assassination operation," the Al-Qassam Brigade posted on Telegram, adding Younis was "among the most important commanders involved in the planning and supervision of the Oct 7 attack".
A security source told AFP shortly after midnight that Younis, the commander of Al-Qassam's Rafah Brigade, died in a strike "targeting him moments ago in Al-Mawasi, west of Khan Younis."
Gaza's civil defence spokesman, Mahmoud Bassal, told AFP the agency had received the body of Younis, 53, and said two people were wounded in the strike in Gaza's south.
Israel and Hamas have accused each other of violating the ceasefire that came into effect in October 2025, after two years of war triggered by the Oct 7 attack.
While the US-backed ceasefire has largely subdued the fighting, Israel has kept up regular strikes in the territory.
More than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the start of the ceasefire, according to the Gaza health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
During the same period, the Israeli military has reported the loss of seven soldiers, as well as one civilian contractor.
Israel's former army chief Gadi Eisenkot is currently locked in negotiations to form a governing coalition while his rival, caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, remains responsible for military operations.

items.title: Elon Musk’s SpaceX Faces Fresh Zelenskyy Backlash Over 161 Kph Starshield Speed Cap
items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Saturday renewed criticism of Elon Musk-led Space Exploration Technologies Corp. NASDAQ:SPCX over speed caps of 161 kph on its Starshield military terminals ...
items.body:
News
/ Benzinga
/ Elon Musk’s SpaceX Faces Fresh Zelenskyy Backlash Over 161 Kph Starshield Speed Cap

Elon Musk’s SpaceX Faces Fresh Zelenskyy Backlash Over 161 Kph Starshield Speed Cap 1 min read

SPCX
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Saturday renewed criticism of Elon Musk -led Space Exploration Technologies Corp. SPCX over speed caps of 161 kph on its Starshield military terminals in occupied territory, hampering air defenses against Russian drones.
According to remarks his office released, Zelenskyy said the limit has been in place for five days. He said it makes it harder to intercept jet-powered Russian drones and leaves cities more exposed.
Zelenskyy Warns of Political Fallout From Starshield Limits
Zelenskyy also warned that keeping restrictions in occupied areas while lifting them elsewhere in Ukraine was extremely dangerous. He said it carried political implications and implied partial non-recognition of those territories as Ukrainian.
He rejected the explanation that the cap is a technical glitch. "We do not believe that is the case," he told reporters.
He said he ordered his top military and foreign ministry officials to address the issue and seek clarification.
SpaceX denied adding restrictions or altering satellite operations, Reuters reported.
SpaceX did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comments.
Second Speed Dispute in Weeks
It is the second such dispute in recent weeks. In mid-October, Ukrainian officials said SpaceX capped Starlink and Starshield speeds at about 160 kph . That followed a sharp turn in U.S.-Ukraine relations. President Donald Trump said Ukraine should get "a new president," a day after announcing a deal to ease sanctions on Russian diesel exports . Service was restored Oct. 24.
Musk said on X that Ukraine’s military violated Starlink’s terms of service . Using Starlink, "a civilian commercial service," for offensive drone strikes "has never been allowed," he said.
The latest disruption follows renewed escalation between Russia and Ukraine, a day after Abu Dhabi talks.
SpaceX has a market capitalization of about $1.89 trillion. Over the past 52 weeks, its stock has traded as high as $225.64 and as low as $104.83. Disclaimer This content was partially produced with the help of AI tools and was reviewed and published by Benzinga editors.

Yoshifumi Takemoto

［東京　１５日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Yoshifumi Takemoto

［東京　１５日　ロイター］ - 城内実経済財政担当相は１５日のＮＨＫ討論番組に出演し、日銀が目標水準に到達したと判断した物価に関連し、足元の物価上昇は海外からのコストプッシュ要因もあると指摘した。その上で「経済成長につながっていく、よい意味での物価上昇になるようなところに持っていくことが必要」と述べ、国内需要が高まる形での物価上昇の必要性を訴えた。

日銀は１０月末公表した「展望リポート（経済物価情勢の展望）」で基調的な物価上昇率が２％目標に到達したとの見解を示していた。

米国のＡＩ（人工知能）関連投資の中核企業である半導体大手エヌビディアのフアンＣＥＯ（最高経営責任者）辞任の影響を問われ、金融市場は不安定な状況だとする一方、内需をしっかり拡大する必要性があると指摘した。「日本が勝ち筋として、フィジカルＡＩや次世代造船、次世代太陽電池などに思い切り投資していくことで、日本の経済成長が膨らむチャンスとしてポジティブに捉えている」と語った。

総額３７０兆円の官民投資を進める成長戦略では１７分野、６２製品・技術を支援対象としているが、「やりっぱなしでなく　発展・成長を見ながら、これ以上国がバックアップしても難しい場合は支援を低減、打ち切る」方針を示し、その基準をどうするか検討中だとした。

items.title: テニス＝アンドレエワとスビトリナが決勝進出、ＷＴＡファイナル
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［インディアンウェルズ（米カリフォルニア州）　１４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［インディアンウェルズ（米カリフォルニア州）　１４日　ロイター］ - 女子テニスのシーズン最終戦、ＷＴＡファイナルは１４日、米カリフォルニア州インディアンウェルズでシングルス準決勝を行い、第３シードでロシア出身のミラ・アンドレエワが決勝に進んだ。

アンドレエワは第５シードのジェシカ・ペグラ（米国）に６─３、６─４でストレート勝ち。重いグラウンドストローク、強力なサーブと粘り強いディフェンスで、初対戦の相手を寄せ付けなかった。

アンドレエワはＷＴＡファイナル初出場ながら、ここまでの４試合で１セットも落としていない。決勝では第６シードのエリナ・スビトリナ（ウクライナ）と対戦する。スビトリナは準決勝で第８シードのリンダ・ノスコバ（チェコ）に６─２、６─１で快勝した。

米国・イスラエルとイランの軍事衝突に伴い、今大会の開催地はリヤドからインディアンウェルズに変更された。

items.title: ラグビー＝日本はイングランドに大敗、ネーションズ選手権
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ロンドン　１４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ロンドン　１４日　ロイター］ - ラグビーの強豪１２カ国・地域で争う国際大会、ネーションズ選手権は１４日、英国のトゥイッケナムなどで試合を行い、世界ランキング１２位の日本代表は同５位のイングランド代表に１５─７８で大敗した。

開始１分でトライを奪われた日本は、その直前のプレーでハリー・ホッキングスが危険なタックルでイエローカードを受け、その後レッドカードに変わって退場処分に。この結果、日本は２０分間の数的不利となった。

日本は大量１３トライを奪われ、イングランド戦での最多失点を喫した。２４歳のウィル・ジョセフがイングランド代表の男子テストマッチ史上最多タイ記録となる１試合５トライをマークした。日本は今大会１勝４敗。イングランドは４勝１敗となった。

日本のエディー・ジョーンズ・ヘッドコーチは、過去に７年率いた古巣との対戦で、相手を混乱させると約束していたが、イングランドの猛攻とホッキングスの退場処分でゲームプランが崩れ去った。

日本は２１日、スコットランドと対戦する。

items.title: ノボの経口肥満治療薬「ウゴービ」、3カ月で体重6.2％減 米リリーからシェア奪還へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ロンドン　１４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ロンドン　１４日　ロイター］ - デンマークの製薬大手ノボノルディスクの経口肥満症治療薬「ウゴービ」の服用を継続した患者の体重が、３カ月で平均６．２％減少したことが分かった。米ワシントンで開催される肥満学会で発表予定の調査結果で明らかになった。

１月のウゴービ発売以来、ノボは米イーライリリーに奪われたシェアの一部を取り戻しつつある。

ノボによると、２０２６年１月５日―２月７日にウゴービの服用を始めた患者は、服用前の平均体重１０３．０キロから平均６．３キロ減量した。全体の約５分の３が５％以上、約６人に１人が１０％以上の減量を達成した。

この調査は、遠隔医療プラットフォーム「Ｒｏ」を利用し、これまでに減量薬を服用したことがなく、ウゴービの服用を３カ月継続した成人５８７２人が対象。

別の研究では、ウゴービが６４週間で約１４％の体重減少をもたらしたのに対し、イーライリリーの経口肥満症治療薬「ファウンダヨ」は７２週間で約１１％の減少にとどまったことが示されている。

items.title: サッカー＝ポルトガル、ロナルド代表引退後初戦でデンマークに大敗
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ブラガ（ポルトガル）　１４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ブラガ（ポルトガル）　１４日　ロイター］ - サッカーの欧州ネーションズリーグ（ＮＬ）は１４日、各地で１次リーグの試合を行い、リーグＡの４組ではクリスティアノ・ロナルドの代表引退後初戦となったポルトガルがデンマークに１─４と大敗した。

ホームのポルトガルは、国歌斉唱の際に選手たちがロナルドの名前と背番号「７」の入ったユニホームを着用し、ファンも「ありがとう、キャプテン」と書かれた横断幕を掲げた。

しかしポルトガルは前半４３分にＰＫで１点を失うと、後半５分、同１２分とラスムス・ホイルンドに立て続けに決められ、同３０分にも失点。同アディショナルタイムにベルナルドシルバが１点を返すにとどまった。

ポルトガルＭＦジョアン・パリーニャは、ポルトガルの放送局「Ｓｐｏｒｔ　ＴＶ」に対し「何もかもがうまくいかなかったという感じだ。正直、なんとも説明がつかない」と話した。

同グループのもう１試合では、ノルウェーがウェールズに３─１で勝利。アントニオ・ヌサとアンドレアス・シェルデルップのゴールで後半２３分までに２点を先行すると、その後１点差に詰め寄られたが、最後はアーリング・ハーランドのＰＫで締めくくった。

ポルトガルは今大会初黒星を喫したが、勝ち点１２で首位をキープ。デンマークが同９で２位、ノルウェーは同６で３位としている。

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［１４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［１４日　ロイター］ - 米女子ゴルフのアニカ・ゲインブリッジ・ペリカンは１４日、フロリダ州ベレアのペリカンＧＣ（パー７０）で第３ラウンドを行い、吉田優利が首位と２打差の３位に浮上した。

９位で出た吉田は４バーディー、１ボギーの３アンダー６７で回り、通算１１アンダーの１９９とした。リンディ・ダンカン（米国）が通算１３アンダーで単独トップ。

原英莉花と岩井明愛は通算６アンダーの１４位、西村優菜と勝みなみは通算５アンダーの１８位となった。４位でスタートした西郷真央は８オーバー７８をたたき、通算２アンダーの３０位に後退。馬場咲希、古江彩佳と並んだ。

岩井千怜は４３位、笹生優花は５２位、竹田麗央と渋野日向子は５９位となった。

items.title: México teme que Stephen Miller complique el acuerdo comercial con EE.UU. por sus exigencias migratorias
items.author: Gonzalo Soto
items.summary: Mientras negociadores mexicanos se centran en reducir el desequilibrio comercial entre ambos países, la prioridad de Miller es disminuir la migración desde México y combatir el crimen organizado.
items.body: Bloomberg — Una figura nueva y poco amistosa se perfila como protagonista en la mesa de negociación donde EE.UU. y México aún intentan cerrar un acuerdo comercial. Como jefe de gabinete de Donald Trump, recientemente ascendido, Stephen Miller goza de una mayor cercanía con el presidente y una capacidad aún mayor para influir en su forma de pensar. Mientras que los negociadores mexicanos se centran en reducir el desequilibrio comercial entre ambos países y fortalecer la competitividad de Norteamérica frente a Asia, la prioridad de Miller es disminuir la migración desde México y combatir el crimen organizado. Ver más: México apostará “al máximo” por producir gas mediante fracking para reducir dependencia con EE.UU. Por ello, la amenaza que Trump lanzó el jueves por la mañana en las redes sociales —de duplicar los aranceles a México si este no toma más medidas para detener los cruces fronterizos indocumentados— no tomó del todo por sorpresa al Gobierno de la presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum. Del lado mexicano, las autoridades ya se estaban preparando para las consecuencias. No está claro qué papel, si es que hubo alguno, desempeñó el artífice de la agresiva agenda de deportaciones de Trump en estas nuevas amenazas. Pero incluso antes de la publicación, las autoridades mexicanas esperaban que el ascenso de Miller prolongara las negociaciones comerciales y aumentara el riesgo de confrontación entre ambas partes, según personas que solicitaron el anonimato para hablar de deliberaciones delicadas. También les preocupa que esto complique el enfoque notoriamente pragmático de Sheinbaum hacia el presidente de EE.UU., basado en refutaciones fundamentadas en datos a las afirmaciones de Trump de que México no está haciendo lo suficiente para satisfacer sus exigencias. El Ministerio de Economía de México se negó a hacer comentarios. Un portavoz de la Casa Blanca no respondió a las preguntas sobre la participación de Miller en las negociaciones comerciales, pero afirmó que las políticas de Trump han dado lugar a la “frontera más segura de la historia”. La postura de la Casa Blanca es que resulta inaceptable que los grupos criminales controlen un vasto territorio en México, incluido el que se extiende a lo largo de la frontera con EE.UU., señaló el portavoz. Ver más: ¿El lunes 16 de noviembre es feriado en México? Si te toca trabajar ese día, así se paga según la ley Está en juego un acuerdo crucial para la economía de México, que depende en gran medida del comercio con EE.UU. y de la inversión procedente de ese país. Los acuerdos para reducir los aranceles sobre el acero y garantizar condiciones actualizadas en el marco del pacto comercial norteamericano conocido como USMCA siguen sin concretarse, a pesar de la disposición de Sheinbaum a imponer gravámenes a los productos chinos y a impulsar la cooperación en materia de seguridad y migración, incluso antes de que Miller asumiera un cargo de mayor responsabilidad en la Casa Blanca. Por ahora, la presidenta que ha insistido en la importancia de mantener la calma ante los arrebatos de Trump en las redes sociales parece comprometida con esa estrategia. El jueves, después de que Trump le pidiera a su gobierno que detuviera las llamadas caravanas de migrantes, Sheinbaum recalcó que ninguna había llegado a la frontera entre Estados Unidos y México desde que él regresó al cargo. Su Gobierno tiene previsto contrarrestar la renovada presión estadounidense con datos que muestran un descenso sostenido de los cruces fronterizos no autorizados y el éxito de las recientes operaciones contra los cárteles de la droga, llevadas a cabo con la ayuda de los servicios de inteligencia estadounidenses, según un funcionario familiarizado con la situación. Sheinbaum, según esta fuente, probablemente seguirá evitando la confrontación directa, al tiempo que hace hincapié en la importancia del comercio bilateral para ambas economías. No obstante, en el seno de la administración de Sheinbaum existe la preocupación de que su postura frente a Trump resulte menos eficaz ante un asesor más ideológico cuya influencia abarca la inmigración, la seguridad fronteriza y la política exterior. Miller ha descrito en repetidas ocasiones la situación en México como una amenaza para la seguridad, comparando a sus cárteles con organizaciones terroristas y argumentando que los grupos criminales controlan partes del país. Las autoridades mexicanas lo consideran un interlocutor especialmente difícil y, en el pasado, han procurado evitarlo, prefiriendo negociar con el representante comercial de EE.UU., Jamieson Greer, u otros funcionarios, según indicaron las fuentes. Según un exfuncionario estadounidense familiarizado con asuntos comerciales, su ascenso al poder no significa que un acuerdo sea imposible. Ver más: Ternium eleva ventas en México por aranceles, pero advierte sobre evasión Pero amenaza con elevar el costo para México, lo que podría obligarlo a hacer mayores concesiones en materia de migración y seguridad, especialmente si Miller insiste en propuestas —como el uso de la fuerza militar estadounidense contra los cárteles de la droga— que México considera una amenaza a su soberanía, dijo el exfuncionario. Según un funcionario mexicano, las reiteradas impugnaciones de Sheinbaum sobre las muertes de ciudadanos mexicanos bajo custodia de inmigración estadounidense podrían conllevar ahora mayores riesgos. Su administración ha presentado 20 denuncias ante fiscales estatales y de condado, ha enviado un informe aparte al Departamento de Justicia y ha remitido más de una docena de notas diplomáticas a Washington. México planea continuar las conversaciones a través del secretario de Comercio, Howard Lutnick, con quien el ministro de Economía, Marcelo Ebrard, ha cultivado una estrecha relación, según informaron varios funcionarios. Pero el secretario de Comercio también se enfrenta ahora a presiones sobre si su departamento hizo lo suficiente para evitar que los chips de inteligencia artificial de Nvidia Corp. ( NVDA ) cayeran en manos de China, lo que plantea dudas sobre su futuro en la administración Trump. Las negociaciones con Lutnick no siempre han sido fluidas. En octubre, el avance en materia de aranceles al acero y al aluminio se ralentizó después de que ejerciera mayor influencia en las conversaciones, lo que mermó las esperanzas mexicanas de que se pudiera alcanzar una solución. items.title: Inversor que puso contra las cuerdas a Argentina ahora libra una batalla en Miami por un puente peatonal
items.author: Michael Smith
items.summary: Newman reside en Miami Beach, donde ocasionalmente realiza trabajos de asesoría y da conferencias, escribe artículos de opinión y, en 2022, publicó Undermoney, una novela que mezcla sexo, espionaje, a ...
items.body: Bloomberg — Jay Newman se hizo conocido en los círculos de los fondos de cobertura por imponerse a Argentina en una dura batalla de 15 años, después de que el país incumpliera sus obligaciones de deuda. Ahora, una década después del enfrentamiento que definió su carrera, Newman, de 74 años, está aplicando ese mismo enfoque implacable y sin contemplaciones a un objetivo muy diferente: los promotores del lujoso edificio de apartamentos de Miami Beach que ahora llama hogar. Ver más: De fenómeno a propietario VIP: el brasileño Ronaldo ficha un ático millonario en Miam El problema no es el apartamento del piso 46 que les compró por US$17,2 millones, sino el puente peatonal que habían prometido construir, pero que nunca hicieron. Los planes contemplaban una llamativa pasarela inspirada en un caleidoscopio, que se elevaría sobre Fifth Street y permitiría a los residentes llegar más rápido a los restaurantes y las boutiques de South Beach. “Van a construir el puente”, dice Newman sin rodeos. En muchos sentidos, es la disputa por excelencia de este momento, mientras neoyorquinos adinerados, como Newman, llegan en masa a Miami y poco a poco se familiarizan con el entorno local y todas sus peculiaridades. Comparado con su batalla multimillonaria contra Argentina, lo que está en juego es insignificante. Y, sin embargo, Newman afirma que el principio es prácticamente el mismo: alguien hizo una promesa y ahora intenta zafarse de ella. Según su versión, no se trata simplemente de una disputa entre los más ricos de los ricos. Es cierto que el puente es muy importante para él —fue una de las razones por las que compró su apartamento en 2024—, pero, asegura, su construcción beneficiará a todos los habitantes de la zona, al permitirles cruzar de forma segura una concurrida vía de acceso y ofrecer una nueva y colorida entrada a Miami Beach. “Sí, esto es como mi nueva Argentina”, dice Newman, quien fue uno de los principales colaboradores del multimillonario Paul Singer en el fondo de cobertura Elliott Management, en una entrevista. Ver más: EFG apuesta por Brasil y Florida para captar riqueza latinoamericana La persistente y, por momentos, casi quijotesca campaña de Newman para exigirle cuentas a Argentina tras el incumplimiento de miles de millones de dólares en bonos se ha convertido en una leyenda entre los fondos de cobertura. Los abogados de Elliott lograron victorias de alto perfil, como el embargo de un buque de guerra argentino de tres mástiles. La entonces presidenta del país, Cristina Fernández de Kirchner, incluso tuvo que recurrir a aviones alquilados para viajar al exterior, ante el temor de que el avión presidencial corriera la misma suerte. Elliott y un grupo de otros gestores de fondos cerraron finalmente un acuerdo histórico de US$4.700 millones, y Newman abandonó la empresa poco después. Actualmente reside en Miami Beach, donde ocasionalmente realiza trabajos de asesoría y da conferencias, escribe artículos de opinión para el Financial Times y, en 2022, publicó Undermoney, una novela que mezcla sexo, espionaje, asesinato y finanzas. Pero Newman, en última instancia, solo podía pasar un tiempo limitado sin meterse en una pelea. El puente formó parte de un acuerdo alcanzado en 2019 con dos de los promotores inmobiliarios más importantes del sur de Florida, David Martin y Russell Galbut. Según el acuerdo, ellos construirían un parque público y supervisarían la construcción del paseo peatonal, mientras que Miami Beach allanaría el camino para la que se convertiría en una de las torres más altas de la ciudad. Diseñado por el artista conceptual francés Daniel Buren, el puente multicolor apareció en los materiales de marketing y en un acuerdo detallado con la ciudad. Miami Beach destinó unos US$10 millones al proyecto, y se espera que el promotor cubra el resto. Ver más: Bradesco Asset expandirá su operación en Miami ante la demanda de activos brasileños Pero a finales de agosto, se declaró imposible construir el puente según el diseño original debido a las líneas eléctricas enterradas bajo el terreno. Los trabajadores habían dañado el revestimiento de un cable principal que suministra electricidad a Miami Beach mientras perforaban los agujeros para los cimientos del puente. En correspondencia con funcionarios municipales, un abogado del promotor se ofreció a ayudar a la ciudad a encontrar otra solución. “Hasta la fecha, no hemos podido encontrar una alternativa segura para construir el puente según el diseño original, y compartimos la decepción de la comunidad”, declaró Martin en un comunicado enviado por correo electrónico a Bloomberg . Añadió que está “comprometido a trabajar en colaboración” con la ciudad en los “próximos pasos”. Para Newman, el intento de la constructora de desentenderse del puente no es un desacuerdo técnico, sino una deuda incumplida. Está enfrentando el problema con la misma determinación que empleó para obligar a Argentina a pagar a los tenedores de sus bonos soberanos en default. Ha movilizado a los vecinos para que presenten quejas ante el alcalde y los concejales en audiencias públicas. Ha criticado al promotor a través de su cuenta personal de Substack. Ha encargado estudios de ingeniería y se ha aliado con Buren, quien escribió una carta mordaz al ayuntamiento. A mediados de octubre, Newman, presidente de la asociación principal de la torre, puso a trabajar a sus abogados. Él y la asociación demandaron al promotor y a Miami Beach ante un tribunal federal de distrito, alegando fraude e infracciones de una ley federal de venta de terrenos, y exigiendo una indemnización por los daños y perjuicios ocasionados por el tramo no construido. Esta era su segunda disputa legal con la empresa, tras un conflicto anterior relacionado con las suites para huéspedes. El promotor sostiene que puede desistir del puente peatonal en determinadas circunstancias. Martin también niega que el cruce fuera una condición para la aprobación de la torre, afirmando que ya había recibido luz verde cuando posteriormente acordaron ayudar a la ciudad a construir el puente. Un abogado que representa a la empresa promotora declaró que la demanda presenta una versión sesgada del proyecto y que esperan aclarar la situación. Newman no se amedrenta y afirma que luchará el tiempo que sea necesario para que se construya el puente. “No tienen salida”, dijo. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

items.title: Weight-loss pill helps patients lose 6% of body weight in three months: data
items.author: Reuters Staff
items.summary: Patients who stayed on Novo Nordisk’s daily Wegovy pill lost an average of 6.2 per cent of their body weight over three months, according to real-world data due to be presented at the ObesityWeek ...
items.body: LONDON -- Patients who stayed on Novo Nordisk’s daily Wegovy pill lost an average of 6.2 per cent of their body weight over three months, according to real-world data due to be presented at the ObesityWeek conference in Washington. The pill, launched in January, has helped Novo regain some ground lost to Eli Lilly, and the Danish drugmaker is trying to stay ahead of its U.S. rival in the race for oral obesity treatments. Novo’s Chief Scientific Officer Martin Holst Lange said in an interview that the real-world data was encouraging as it broadly replicated the findings of 5.5 per cent weight loss at 12 weeks seen in Novo’s late-stage trial for the pill. Study participants, who started taking the pill between January 5 and February 7, 2026, lost an average of 6.3 kg (13.9 pounds) from a baseline weight of 103.0 kg (227 pounds), Novo said. About three-fifths lost at least 5 per cent of their weight, and roughly one in six lost at least 10 per cent. The analysis covered 5,872 adults on the Ro telehealth platform who had never taken a weight-loss drug and who stayed on the pill for the full three months. Novo Nordisk’s fortunes have declined significantly since it became Europe’s most valuable listed company following the 2021 launch of its injectable weight-loss drug, Wegovy. Its stock has plummeted over 70 per cent from its peak as Lilly surpassed it to take the lead in the obesity-drug market. According to company presentations earlier this month, however, oral treatments now represent roughly a third of U.S. obesity prescriptions, with Novo securing over 80 per cent of new oral prescriptions. The company in September said separate real-world data showed patients who switched from weight-loss injections to Novo’s pill continued to lose weight. Oral Wegovy — known chemically as semaglutide — led to about a 14 per cent reduction in body weight over 64 weeks, while Eli Lilly’s obesity pill Foundayo led to about an 11 per cent reduction over 72 weeks, separate studies have shown. Reporting by Patrick Wingrove in London; Editing by Tomasz Janowski, Reuters

items.title: スペースＸ「スターシップ」、発射塔のアームで上段部分の初回収に成功　完全再利用へ前進
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［米テキサス州スターベース　１４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［米テキサス州スターベース　１４日　ロイター］ - 米実業家イーロン・マスク氏率いる宇宙開発企業スペースＸの次世代ロケット「スターシップ」が１４日、２２時間の地球周回軌道飛行から帰還し、テキサス州の発射塔に設置された巨大なアームによってロケットの上段部分が初めて回収された。今回の回収成功は、同社が１０年かけて開発を進めてきた完全再利用可能なロケットにとって不可欠なものとみられている。

スターシップは２６基のスターリンク衛星を軌道上に展開。上段部分は地球を１４周した後、同州スターベースにあるスペースＸの発射場上空の厚い雲の中から姿を現した。機体を垂直に反転させるためエンジンを再点火し、轟音を立てながら、発射塔に設置された「メカジラ」と呼ばれるアームに向かってゆっくり降下した。

下段部分の回収には失敗した。

マスク氏は、スターシップをスペースＸの収益性の高いスターリンク衛星事業の将来の主力機と見なしており、軌道上にデータセンターを設置したり、人類を月へ帰還させたり、最終的には火星に定住させたりといった野望を実現するための重要な手段と位置付けている。

items.title: サッカー＝国際親善試合で日本がブラジルに競り勝つ、坂元が決勝点
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［１４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［１４日　ロイター］ - サッカーの日本代表は１４日、シンガポールで国際親善試合を行い、ブラジル代表に３─２で競り勝った。後半アディショナルタイムに坂元達裕が決勝ゴールを奪った。

世界ランキング１７位の日本は前半１５分、堂安律のスルーパスで抜け出した久保建英が左足で決めて先制。さらにその４分後、右サイドからの中野就斗のクロスを受けた中村敬斗がゴール隅に流し込み、世界ランク６位の相手を２─０とリードした。

日本は同３３分と後半３０分にビニシウス・ジュニオールにゴールを決められて追い付かれたが、途中出場の坂元がアディショナルタイム１分に決勝ゴール。南野拓実のブロックの後、こぼれ球を拾った佐野海舟が持ち込み、最後はゴール前の混戦の中で坂元が浮かせたシュートを決めた。

日本は６月に行われたワールドカップ（Ｗ杯）北中米３カ国大会の決勝トーナメント１回戦では、ブラジルに１─２の逆転負けを喫していた。日本は１７日にパラグアイと対戦。８年余りチームを指揮した森保一監督は、この試合を最後に退任する。

items.title: 野球＝日本が豪州に七回コールド勝ちで決勝進出、アジアプロ野球
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［１４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［１４日　ロイター］ - 野球のアジアプロ野球チャンピオンシップは１４日、東京ドームで１次リーグの２試合を行い、日本はオーストラリアに１６─１で圧勝。七回コールドゲームで３連勝として決勝に進んだ。

日本は一回表に打者１５人の猛攻で一挙１１得点を挙げた。相手のエラーで１点を先制した後、指名打者の山口航輝、渡部聖弥内野手が連続タイムリー。その後も３者連続の押し出し四球などで７─０とし、宗山塁内野手が満塁本塁打でさらにリードを広げた。

二回には正木智也内野手、三回には渡部が２ランを放った。先発の武内夏暉投手は４回を投げて１安打、ソロ本塁打による１失点に抑えた。大会３連覇を目指す日本は１５日の決勝で韓国と対戦する。３位決定戦では台湾とオーストラリアが戦う。

この日のもう１試合では、韓国が台湾に６─４で勝利。オーストラリア、台湾と１勝２敗で並んだが、得失点率差（１イニング当たりの得点率と失点率の差）で韓国が勝ち上がった。

items.title: 米航空便、15日夜に正常化へ　保守作業の不具合原因か
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
David Shepardson

[ワシントン １４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
David Shepardson

[ワシントン １４日 ロイター] - ベッドフォード米連邦航空局（ＦＡＡ）長官は１４日、全米の空港で航空機の離陸が停止された問題について、通常の運航ダイヤに戻るのは１５日夜遅くになるとの見通しを示した。運航は徐々に回復しており、当局は定期保守作業中の不具合が原因だったとしている。

ＦＡＡは１３日、航空管制センターで通信障害が発生したとして、全米の空港で航空機の地上待機命令を発出。航空情報サイトのフライトアウェアによると、同日は約９２００便が欠航、約７５００便が遅延した。米国東部時間午後９時３５分現在（０２３５ＧＭＴ、日本時間午前１１時３５分）時点で、１４日の欠航は６４００便超、遅延は約８０００便となった。

ベッドフォード氏は混乱について謝罪するとともに、システムは現時点で安定していると語った。

ホワイトハウスは１３日、危機管理室で緊急会合を開き、連邦政府機関はサイバー攻撃かどうかの確認に追われた。しかし、ダフィー運輸長官は１４日、問題の発端はＦＡＡの請負業者Ｌ３ハリスが遠隔地の施設で少なくとも１台の新しいルーターを設置した作業にあったと説明した。

同長官は会見で「ユーザーの操作ミスなのか、Ｌ３ハリスによる設置ミスなのか、あるいはルーターに欠陥があったのか、原因を特定するために調査を進めている。現時点では何が原因だったのかを特定できていない」と述べた。

同長官によると、障害は１３日の午後、管制センターでレーダーおよび通信システムが不安定となったことから始まった。当局者によると、ルーターの問題により他の通信センターにデータが過剰に流入したことが原因。同長官は「４─５秒ごとに１０００件以上の接続試行があり、その結果、航空機との通信に問題が生じ、レーダーにも一部障害が発生した」と付け加えた。

INDIAN WELLS, California, Nov 14 : Aryna Sabalenka apologised on Saturday for her angry outburst during her defeat by Ukraine's Elina Svitolina at the WTA Finals.
Television footage appeared to show the Belarusian swearing during Friday's round-robin match, with some social media users interpreting her remarks as being directed at Svitolina or Ukrainians. The loss eliminated Sabalenka from the season-ending tournament.
"My comment was not directed at Elina," Sabalenka said in a social media post.
"I was frustrated with a small group of spectators who were aggressively cheering my mistakes, and I reacted emotionally in the moment.

"That said, I should have handled my frustration differently, and I apologise to anyone I offended.
"Elina played a great match, and I wish her all the best for the rest of the tournament."
Svitolina did not shake hands with Sabalenka after the match, maintaining her policy of not doing so with Russian or Belarusian opponents following Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, which Moscow launched with Belarus as a staging ground. 
Asked about her reaction to Sabalenka's apology, Svitolina called for mutual respect, acknowledging that fans' passions can sometimes run high.
"We've played many times with Aryna. She has her fans, I have my fans," she told reporters after her semi-final win over Linda Noskova on Saturday.
She expressed hope that matches between the two of them would be respected, "because yes, sometimes in some matches that we've played, also been not great comments towards me in regards of the war."

items.title: Motherson eyes bigger India play with global technologies to drive growth
items.summary: The strategy is part of its broader Vision 2030 ambition to achieve USD 108 billion in topline gross revenue by 2029-30 ...
items.body:
Home / Companies / News / Motherson eyes bigger India play with global technologies to drive growth

Motherson eyes bigger India play with global technologies to drive growth The strategy is part of its broader Vision 2030 ambition to achieve USD 108 billion in topline gross revenue by 2029-30

Representative Image | Photo: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India New Delhi 4 min read Last Updated : Nov 15 2026 | 12:31 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Auto components major Samvardhana Motherson International Ltd (SAMIL) aims to leverage technologies acquired through its global expansion to tap emerging opportunities in India's automotive market, as higher product standards and the shift to stricter emission norms drive demand for advanced solutions.
The strategy is part of its broader Vision 2030 ambition to achieve USD 108 billion in topline gross revenue by 2029-30.
In an interview with PTI, Pankaj Mital, Whole-time Director and President, and Gandharv Tongia, Group Chief Financial Officer, outlined the company's growth priorities, including bringing globally acquired technologies to India, expanding its presence across business segments and geographies, and strengthening its customer relationships.
 

"We believe that India's growth will also benefit us significantly, particularly because we now own many technologies. The quality of products being manufactured and consumed in India is improving, and the country is also moving towards the latest emission norms," Mital said.
"With the acquisitions we have made, we have gained access to new technologies. We are delivering solutions that meet the standards of the best in the world, and these technologies are now part of our portfolio. We can therefore bring them to India and provide the best solutions to the market," he added.
Also Read

Why Ola Electric is closing stores and turning to dealer-led retail network

Festive demand, export recovery drive auto sector growth, says MOFSL

2026 set for record auto sales, likely to touch 32 million units: Fada

Tata Motors plans local assembly of Iveco vehicles, eyes global expansion

Tata Motors PV sales rise 23% to 75,426 units in Oct on strong demand

On the domestic growth outlook, Tongia said India's automotive industry had maintained double-digit growth since the GST relaxation and the company expected the broader momentum to continue.

"India, as you know, the growth rate of our industry has been in double digits since the time the GST relaxation was done. By and large, we anticipate that the industry will continue to grow. It's possible that a quarter here and there might impact the performance, but structurally India is a consumption powerhouse and we anticipate that the growth level continues in India in times to come," Tongia said.
He also said Motherson had a strong balance sheet and order book, supported by both organic and inorganic business additions, as it works towards its longer-term revenue ambition.
"We are targeting a topline gross revenue of USD 108 billion in 2030. As mentioned, our balance sheet is very strong. We have a very strong order book organically as well as inorganically. We will continue to meet and exceed customer expectations and we are optimistic on our outlook," Tongia said.

Mital said the company's acquisition strategy would continue to be driven by customer requirements, with joint ventures and acquisitions considered when customers need solutions that the group cannot provide independently.
"For us, the key consideration has always been what the customer wants. If our customers require solutions that we cannot provide on our own, we look at joint ventures or acquisitions to address those needs. Most of our acquisitions have been customer-led," he said.
"Whether the requirement is in technology, in an area where we already operate, or in a completely new domain, you will not find us lacking in our efforts to find solutions for our customers," he added.

The group is also seeking to reduce its exposure to demand fluctuations in individual markets through diversification across automotive segments, geographies and newer verticals, while increasing its content per vehicle and adding new customers.
"When we look at demand, we are well diversified and continue to add more segments to our portfolio. We have increased our content per vehicle. In the automotive segment, we have added new customers and expanded our presence in geographies where we were not present a year ago. We are also entering new verticals," Mital said.
"Our 3CX10 strategy is always in play. That is how we plan for the group and focus on building diversification. If one segment is facing a downturn in a particular geography, we can still find solutions for ourselves in other segments or markets," he said.

On rising copper prices, Tongia said the company's wiring harness business, which accounts for around 30 per cent of group revenue, had contractual arrangements that allow changes in input costs to be passed on to customers at quarterly or six-monthly intervals.
"Copper has risen sharply in recent times. In the wiring harness business, we have a contractual arrangement with our consumers, under which we can increase or decrease costs on a quarterly or six-monthly basis. So, to that extent, we don't expect any significant impact on our profitability because of copper prices," he said.
