items.title: From bicycle parts to satellites: Inside Sunil Mittal's 50-year journey
items.summary: As Bharti Enterprises marks 50 years, Sunil Mittal outlines plans to expand Airtel into AI, cloud, digital finance and satellite services ...
items.body:
Home / Companies / People / From bicycle parts to satellites: Inside Sunil Mittal's 50-year journey

From bicycle parts to satellites: Inside Sunil Mittal's 50-year journey As Bharti Enterprises marks 50 years, Sunil Mittal outlines plans to expand Airtel into AI, cloud, digital finance and satellite services

Bharti Enterprises chairman Sunil Bharti Mittal | Photo: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India New Delhi 12 min read Last Updated : Nov 15 2026 | 12:26 PM IST

Listen to This Article

When Sunil Bharti Mittal set up a small manufacturing unit making bicycle parts in Ludhiana in 1976, he was barely 18. Fifty years later, the founder of Bharti Enterprises is presiding over a business empire whose flagship, Bharti Airtel, has become one of the world's largest telecommunications companies.
The journey from bicycle crankshafts to mobile networks, submarine cables and satellite communications has been marked by bets that often ran ahead of the market, setbacks triggered by policy changes and three major crises that Mittal describes as Bharti's "Mahabharatas".
Now, as the group marks its 50th anniversary, Mittal is preparing for another transformation. He wants Airtel to evolve from a telecommunications operator into a digitally enabled technology company, with connectivity at its core and businesses spanning artificial intelligence, sovereign cloud, digital finance and satellite services.
 

His prescription for India's digital economy is equally expansive: higher mobile tariffs, financially stronger telecom operators, a substantial expansion of network infrastructure and greater national control over strategic communications systems.
The most immediate part of that agenda concerns what consumers pay for mobile services. Mittal believes average revenue per user, or ARPU, in India should rise to about ₹350 a month against the ₹300 benchmark he advocated roughly a decade ago. Rising operating costs and the investment needed to expand digital infrastructure justify the higher level, he said.
Also Read

India must hold satellite 'kill switch', avoid reliance on one firm: Mittal

Sunil Bharti Mittal awarded France's Legion of Honour for business ties

Ahead of Starlink in queue for satcom nod, says Sunil Bharti Mittal

AI shouldn't be stifled, but unchecked use will be 'foolish': Sunil Mittal

France confers highest civilian honour on Bharti Enterprises' Sunil Mittal

"Everything is up. So, 350 would be the right ARPU for our industry," Mittal told PTI in an interview.

He compared the cost of mobile services with everyday purchases. "Now, you buy soap and a packet of chips. You know what it costs. Having a bottle of Pepsi costs you a lot more than that".
At ₹10-12 a day, he argued, consumers receive access not only to calls and data but also to banking, education, healthcare records, direct benefit transfers, UPI payments and entertainment. "I think you can't say that is not affordable."   Airtel reported mobile ARPU of ₹271 in the September quarter, up from ₹256 a year earlier. Reaching Mittal's proposed level would require about a 29 per cent increase from the latest figure. The last major industry-wide tariff revision came in June 2024, when operators raised prices by around 10-25 per cent. Mittal did not give a timeline for reaching ₹350, saying, "I don't know".

FROM A BICYCLE CRANKSHAFT TO MOBILE PHONES Mittal's first venture was a modest manufacturing operation in Ludhiana, making bicycle components for the city's established bicycle industry.
"I was only 18 at that time, and I started with manufacturing, not trading in bicycle parts, which, as you know, Ludhiana is pretty famous for," he recalled.
"The dream is to sort of, you know, do something, create something for yourself, make your ends meet, and get enough fuel to fire your ambitions or dreams that one has at that time and age," he said.
Bicycle parts were followed by hosiery and stainless steel sheets. Mittal then moved into importing and trading products that were relatively new to Indian consumers, including portable generators, push-button telephones, cordless phones, answering machines and fax machines.

"They were flying off the shelves. The margins were good," he said.
But an early success also brought a lesson in the risks of doing business in India's tightly controlled economy. His portable generator business, which had become highly profitable, collapsed after the government changed its import policy.
"Generator business, which was a very thriving, successful business for a few years, just went out overnight because the policy changed," he said.
Having already built a business around telephone equipment, Mittal saw mobile services as the next step in communications. He had observed the development of cellular telephony in markets such as Britain and France and believed India would eventually embrace the technology, despite the high cost of handsets and services.

Bharti launched Airtel's mobile services in Delhi in 1995. The market was then in its infancy, with mobile phones largely beyond the reach of ordinary consumers. An agency survey had estimated that Delhi would have only 10,000 mobile subscribers in 10 years.
"I knew that was not going to be the case," Mittal said. Airtel crossed that number within its first year.
Even he had not anticipated how deeply mobile phones would transform everyday life. "Nobody could have imagined" that mobile telephony would become the "fabric of everybody's lives", he said. Airtel's early slogan was "Power to keep in touch". There was not even an SMS service at the time.

THE BET ON MARKETS RIVALS QUESTIONED One of the defining decisions in Airtel's expansion was its push beyond major cities into smaller towns and difficult markets, where demand was uncertain, and network deployment was more challenging.
Mittal recalled that Hutchison's then chief executive, Hashim Ghosh, questioned the strategy.
"You're making a big mistake going into these places. They will not have enough demand," Ghosh told him, according to Mittal.
Airtel nevertheless pursued a pan-India presence, investing in markets including Bihar, Odisha, Assam and the northeast. In some of these regions, Mittal said, the company was, for some time, the only operator.
"That's what I would say gave us the scale and the confidence to keep growing the business," he said.

The strategy was based on the expectation that falling tariffs and rising affordability would unlock demand well beyond affluent urban consumers. The subsequent expansion of mobile telephony across the country vindicated the decision and helped Airtel build a nationwide network.
Another consequential decision concerned how the company would manage that network. When Airtel had around four to five million subscribers and wanted to expand to 25-35 million, it recognised that building all the necessary engineering, information technology and operational capabilities in-house would be difficult.
Bharti vice-chairman Akhil Gupta proposed outsourcing network and IT operations to specialist vendors. The idea faced internal resistance, but Mittal backed it.

The model allowed Airtel to focus on customers, marketing and business strategy, while external partners took responsibility for much of the network equipment and its management. It drew surprise and criticism from international telecom peers before becoming a reference point for other operators.
"It eventually became a Harvard case study, and a lot of companies followed that model later on," Mittal said.
Bharti also invested ahead of demand in long-distance networks, enterprise connectivity and submarine cable infrastructure. Mittal described the Chennai-Singapore cable, built during the tenure of Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, as India's first such project.
THREE MAJOR BATTLES AND THE JIO DISRUPTION The expansion was not without existential challenges. Mittal has identified 2002, 2009 and 2016 as three particularly difficult periods for Bharti, describing them as the company's "Mahabharatas".

The 2016 crisis coincided with Reliance Jio's entry into the market, when free introductory services and aggressive pricing triggered a price war and accelerated consolidation. Several operators exited or merged, while surviving companies faced pressure to invest in networks and retain customers.
Mittal credits employees with helping Airtel withstand the disruption, recalling frontline teams engaging customers across states even as rivals offered free services.
"In our case, our raw material was not the balance sheet. It was not the technology, because ultimately, it is the same technology. It was our people," he said.
The upheaval left India with a far smaller number of major operators.
Mittal believes the country should not return to the era when more than a dozen companies competed for subscribers.
"India went too far into over a dozen operators," he said, arguing that fragmentation weakened balance sheets, divided spectrum and reduced the industry's capacity to invest.
He considers three private operators, alongside state-owned BSNL, an appropriate structure for India. The comments come as Vodafone Idea continues to face financial challenges and BSNL works to rebuild its network and competitive position.
Telecommunications, he said, is no longer simply a business of voice calls and data. UPI payments, banking, healthcare records, government benefit transfers, e-commerce, delivery platforms and streaming services all depend on reliable connectivity.
Mittal also argued that existing networks have room to accommodate more customers and traffic.
"All of us are running at 20, 30 per cent of our capacity of networks. So, we can take more traffic, we can take more customers," he said.
TELCOS SEEK A BIGGER SHARE OF DIGITAL VALUE Mittal's call for stronger operators is linked to what he sees as an imbalance in the digital economy: telecom companies bear the cost of building spectrum, towers, fibre and network infrastructure, while online platforms often command much higher valuations.
"We do all the hard work, but we don't get the same valuation and the profitability that those who don't make these investments get," he said.
He cited the valuations of companies such as Google, Facebook and Netflix, as well as e-commerce, quick-commerce and streaming platforms that rely on telecom networks to reach customers.
The issue reflects a longstanding tension in the global telecom industry, where operators make large, recurring capital investments while much of the commercial value generated by rising internet use is captured by digital services.
Mittal welcomed Reliance Jio's recent listing, saying it would bring greater investor attention and research coverage to the sector. But he said the listing had no direct bearing on Airtel's valuation, which he described as already placing it among a relatively small group of global telecom companies valued above $100 billion.
5G'S REVENUE SHORTFALL AND THE NEXT TECHNOLOGY CYCLE Despite investment in next-generation networks, Mittal acknowledged that 5G has not delivered the new revenue streams operators had expected, particularly from industrial applications such as connected factories and automation.
"That's been a disappointment globally," he said.
The rollout has involved spectrum expenditure running into lakhs of crores of rupees across operators, with network deployment costs estimated by Mittal at another ₹1.5 lakh crore.
He nevertheless sees the investment as necessary to support future demand.
The next opportunity could emerge from 6G and what he described as "sensing networks", potentially taking shape over the next three to five years.
In that environment, connected glasses, rings, watches and earpods could perform functions now handled by smartphones, and networks would increasingly interact with users' artificial intelligence agents.
For Airtel, the ambition is to build businesses around growing demand for connectivity and computing rather than depend principally on mobile subscriptions and tariffs.
Asked what the company might look like a decade from now, Mittal said: "It will be a digitally enabled technology company where connectivity will be at its core because everything will need connectivity".
The vision includes digital financial services, sovereign cloud infrastructure, AI computing, fibre connections to homes and satellite links for remote areas. Mittal believes India has the potential to develop capabilities in artificial intelligence, large language models, quantum computing and space technology.
But that will require a substantial expansion of physical infrastructure.
India has around 350,000 mobile towers, compared to more than one million in China, he said, arguing that the country needs to double its tower base at least. More fibre, submarine cables, satellites and AI data centres will also be required.
SATELLITES AND STRATEGIC AUTONOMY Satellite communications are another part of Mittal's strategy through Eutelsat OneWeb, in which Bharti has invested. The low-Earth-orbit network is intended to connect remote villages, forests, mountains, ships and aircraft where conventional mobile and fibre networks cannot economically reach.
Mittal recalled persuading the British government to commit $500 million to the venture during the pandemic and said he subsequently invested $1 billion of his own money.
He sees satellite services as complementary to terrestrial networks, rather than a substitute for them.
"Where there is fibre, radio cannot compete with it. Where there is a radio, satellite cannot compete with it," he said.
The commercial opportunity is only one part of the case. Mittal argues that satellite communications are increasingly important to national security, particularly as conflicts demonstrate the role of space-based connectivity in military operations.
"The kill switch, as we call it, should not be sitting somewhere else.
India must have control over its own space destiny," he said.
He believes India needs multiple satellite providers, oversight of equipment and systems entering the country, and control over how data is routed. The position reflects growing concerns among governments about dependence on foreign-controlled communications infrastructure.
Mittal said OneWeb services were functioning, with the company awaiting the final government signal to expand commercial operations. He cited the use of terminals for emergency services and recalled economic adviser Sanjeev Sanyal using one during a boat journey to Oman.
THE BUSINESSES BHARTI LEFT BEHIND Mittal's career has also involved exits from businesses that did not become central to the group's strategy. Bharti entered modern retail through a partnership with Walmart and expanded into insurance through international partnerships, but eventually stepped back from those ventures.
The Walmart venture faced resistance in India and did not develop as originally envisaged.
"Walmart was literally blocked out of this country," Mittal said, adding that the American retailer later returned through its acquisition of Flipkart.
Bharti also sold its general insurance business to ICICI Lombard and is bringing Prudential in as a partner in life insurance.
Asked whether he regretted leaving businesses behind, Mittal said: "There are no regrets. We were too busy building our telecom story".
The response reflects his emphasis on concentrating capital and management attention on businesses where the group believes it can build scale.
Fifty years after starting with a single bicycle component, Mittal's ambitions now extend to the infrastructure underpinning artificial intelligence, cloud computing and space-based communications. His central argument is that India's digital economy will require more investment in networks and stronger operators - even if that means consumers paying more for mobile services.
The entrepreneur who once bet that mobile phones would find millions of customers beyond the major cities is now making a broader wager: that connectivity will remain the foundation of a much larger technology economy.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

items.summary: An IndiGo flight from Pune to Guwahati with 192 persons on board returned to Pune airport on Sunday after its landing gear failed to retract shortly after take-off, airport officials said. IndiGo ...
items.body:
Home / Industry / Aviation / News / Guwahati-bound IndiGo flight returns to Pune due to technical issue

Guwahati-bound IndiGo flight returns to Pune due to technical issue IndiGo flight 6E 0623 (VT-IZE) reported a technical issue soon after taking off from Pune airport

Following the landing, the aircraft was escorted to Bay No. 7 by three fire-fighting vehicles and two ambulances as part of the prescribed emergency response procedures | Image: Bloomberg

Press Trust of India Pune 2 min read Last Updated : Nov 15 2026 | 12:06 PM IST

Listen to This Article

An IndiGo flight from Pune to Guwahati with 192 persons on board returned to Pune airport on Sunday after its landing gear failed to retract shortly after take-off, airport officials said.
IndiGo flight 6E 0623 (VT-IZE) reported a technical issue soon after taking off from Pune airport.
The pilot informed the Air Traffic Control (ATC) that the aircraft's landing gear (undercarriage) failed to retract and remained in the extended position, the Pune airport authorities said in a statement.
Following the information, Pune airport authorities immediately coordinated with the ATC, IndiGo and other agencies concerned. The Indian Air Force (IAF), which manages the airport, declared a "full emergency", following which all prescribed emergency response procedures were activated, they said.
  Fire services, ambulance services and other emergency response teams were placed on high alert to deal with any eventuality and ensure the safety of passengers and crew, the statement said.
Also Read

Microsoft service disruption impacts IndiGo's email support services

IndiGo in talks with Brazilian planemaker Embraer to buy 100 jets

IndiGo, Asian Paints, IOC: Analyst view on crude sensitives as oil dips 13%

IndiGo CEO seeks lower Mumbai airport charges after Terminal 1 revamp

As part of the precautionary measures, the aircraft conducted a low pass over the runway to facilitate a visual assessment of its landing gear. After the assessment, the aircraft landed safely at Pune airport at 9.04 am, officials said.
Following the landing, the aircraft was escorted to Bay No. 7 by three fire-fighting vehicles and two ambulances as part of the prescribed emergency response procedures.
After confirming that the aircraft was in a safe and normal condition, the ATC withdrew the full emergency at 9.10 am, the officials said.
Subsequently, the aerobridge was connected to the aircraft and all passengers were safely deboarded.
"All 192 persons on board, including passengers and crew, were safe and no injuries were reported," the statement said.
Meanwhile, IndiGo was arranging an alternate aircraft from Bengaluru to Pune to facilitate the onward journey of the affected passengers to Guwahati, it added.

items.title: Figure Skating-Malinin opens season in style with Skate America title
items.summary: Three-time world champion Ilia Malinin claimed the Skate America title in Everett on Saturday, winning the event for a fourth time and delighting audiences with a choreo spin inspired by his mother.
items.body:
Figure Skating-Malinin opens season in style with Skate America title
Reuters | Updated: 15-11-2026 12:06 IST | Created: 15-11-2026 12:06 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways
AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Three-time world champion Ilia Malinin claimed the Skate America title in Everett on Saturday, winning the event for a fourth time and delighting audiences with a choreo spin inspired by his mother. It marked a successful start to a campaign in which Malinin is seeking to balance the technical difficulty he is known for with greater artistic expression.
The American finished with a total score of 284.31 points after topping the short program on Friday and placing second in the free skate, securing victory by 9.58 points over Italy's Daniel Grassl. Grassl produced the strongest free skate of the event, climbing from fourth after the short program to finish with 274.73, while Israel's Tamir Kuperman completed the podium on with 248.55 in his senior Grand Prix debut.
Performing his "Blue Eye Samurai" free skate, Malinin overcame a slightly awkward landing on his opening quad flip before nailing a triple Axel and quad toe loop. The 21-year-old, nicknamed the "Quad God", then landed a quad Lutz-triple Axel-double Axel combination, adding a triple Lutz-double toe loop and a quad Salchow before bringing the crowd to its feet with his trademark backflip.
He opted against attempting his signature quadruple Axel, instead delighting the crowd with a choreo spin. "It was definitely the most fun I've ever had, but skating that program, man, I'm tired," Malinin told NBC.
"My legs, at the end of the program, just nearly gave up on me, but I'm glad I was able to stay on my feet most of the time, and I'm just looking forward to how the program progresses in the future." Malinin said his mother Tatiana Malinina, the 1999 Grand Prix Final champion, was a constant source of inspiration.
"She's been there for me ever since I was born, and I always appreciate everything she does for me," he said. Malinin had a roller-coaster 2025-26 season. He saw his 14-event winning streak end at the Winter Olympics, where he finished eighth in the singles event, before rebounding weeks later to capture a third consecutive world title.
Malinin will return to action at the NHK Trophy in Japan in two weeks, where a podium finish is expected to secure his place at December's Grand Prix Final, an event he has won in each of the last three seasons.

DUBLIN, Nov 14 : Ireland secured an emphatic 43-15 victory over Fiji in the Nations Championship on Saturday to stay in contention for a place in the final of the new competition.
Ireland were 17-15 ahead at halftime and stretched their lead after the break to move to 20 points in the Northern Hemisphere standings, level with England and a point behind France.
Wingers Tommy O’Brien and Robert Baloucoune scored two tries each with Ronan Kelleher, Andrew Porter and Nick Tominey getting the other three.
Fiji’s two tries came with four minutes midway through the first half from Josua Tuisova and captain Peceli Yato.

Ireland were wary of the danger of another upset in the Nations Championship after New Zealand and South Africa were beaten this weekend, but O’Brien went over in the eighth minute to settle their nerves.
Fiji’s double strike put them 12-7 ahead, however, before right wing Baloucoune went over twice in the last 10 minutes of the first half.
Ben Volavola’s penalty on the stroke of halftime reduced Ireland’s lead to two points but after the interval the gulf in quality became more apparent.
Ireland stretched their lead when Kelleher scored from a lineout maul and Porter placed the ball over the line from a simple tap-and-go.
Fiji’s desperation to stay in the contest led to many mistakes and Ireland took advantage in the 59th minute as Sam Prendergast sent a superb grubber kick through for O’Brien to pounce on before Timoney completed the rout.
Ireland must now beat South Africa and hope France, who host Argentina, and England, who take on New Zealand, falter in Saturday’s matches to secure a place in the final at Twickenham on November 29.

BRAGA, Portugal, Nov 14 : Portugal's first match since Cristiano Ronaldo's international retirement ended in a crushing 4-1 home defeat by Denmark in the Nations League on Saturday, with Rasmus Hojlund scoring twice as a night of tributes in Braga turned sour for Jorge Jesus and his players.
Norway beat Wales 3-1 in Oslo in the other League A Group Four match, with Antonio Nusa and Andreas Schjelderup scoring before Erling Haaland's late penalty sealed victory.
Portugal remain top on 12 points, three ahead of Denmark, with Norway third on six and Wales bottom on three. One round of league-phase matches remains, with Wales hosting Portugal and Denmark at home to Norway on Tuesday.
In front of a packed stadium, Portugal's players wore shirts bearing Ronaldo's name and number seven during the national anthem.

Supporters unfurled a banner reading "Obrigado, capi7ão" — "Thank you, captain" — alongside images of him lifting the European Championship and Nations League trophies.
Ronaldo announced his international retirement on social media last week following a public falling-out with manager Jesus.
DENMARK RUN RIOT
Portugal dominated much of the first half in pouring rain but fell behind shortly before halftime.
Hojlund had a header ruled out for a foul by Joachim Andersen in the build-up before another aerial effort struck Ruben Dias’ hand. Following a VAR intervention and pitchside review, the referee awarded a penalty which Denmark captain Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg drove into the top-right corner shortly before halftime.
Hojlund doubled Denmark's advantage five minutes after the interval, slipping behind the defence to meet a cross from the right with a powerful volley.
The striker scored again seven minutes later, cutting inside Renato Veiga on a counter-attack before firing a right-footed shot past Diogo Costa from the edge of the box.
Andersen completed the rout in the 75th minute, rising to power home a towering header from i.nside the area after Mathias Jensen delivered a free kick from the right.
Bernardo Silva scored a consolation goal for Portugal three minutes into added time, firing home from close range after the goalkeeper parried the ball.
“Practically everything went wrong for us... It’s actually hard to find an explanation," midfielder Joao Palhinha told Portuguese broadcaster Sport TV. 
"It was an unlucky night for us; we made it far too easy for our opponents. We’ve got a match on Tuesday, so we’ve got until then to reflect about what happened today. But I have no doubt whatsoever that we’ll bounce back and secure top spot in the group in Wales.”
NORWAY PUNISH WALES
After a subdued first half at Ullevaal Stadion, Nusa broke the deadlock in the 59th minute with a half-volley from the edge of the area following a partially cleared corner.
Schjelderup doubled the lead two minutes after coming off the bench. Nusa raced down the left and fed Haaland, who squared for the substitute to tap into an empty net at the far post.
David Brooks gave Wales hope in the 79th minute, racing onto a through ball and chipping the advancing goalkeeper despite pressure from a defender.
But Connor Roberts fouled Schjelderup inside the area six minutes later and Haaland converted the resulting penalty in the 88th minute to secure Norway's win.

INDIAN WELLS, California, Nov 14 : Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva extended her unbeaten run at the WTA Finals on Saturday, dispatching American Jessica Pegula 6-3 6-4 to reach the final, where she will face a resurgent Elina Svitolina.
Andreeva's heavy groundstrokes, strong serving and tireless defense were too much for the American in their first career meeting, played under sunny skies in the California desert.
"It was a tough match," Andreeva said. "You have to work hard to win a point against her. She is going to leave everything out there and make your life complicated, so I wanted to make her life complicated as well today."
The opening set was tight until Andreeva pounced on a looping shot from Pegula and drilled a forehand winner to break serve for a 5-3 lead.

Pegula, backed by a supportive crowd, earned break points as Andreeva served for the set, but shanked an overhead and Andreeva took the set two points later when her opponent's backhand found the net.
Pegula broke to grab a 3-1 advantage in the second set but the lead would prove short-lived. Andreeva broke straight back with a deft volley and broke again to lead 4-3. The tournament's third seed ultimately sealed the win when a Pegula backhand sailed long on match point.
Andreeva, making her WTA Finals debut, has not dropped a set in four matches at the event.
SVITOLINA SHINES
She will face sixth seed Elina Svitolina in Sunday's final after the Ukrainian needed just over an hour to cruise past Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova 6-2 6-1 in Saturday's other semi-final.
Despite strong sun shining in her eyes, Svitolina delivered a crosscourt backhand winner to claim the first set.
She raced out to a 5-0 lead in the second and raised her arms in triumph and beamed a smile after Noskova's forehand went wide on match point.
Andreeva holds a 2-1 lead in their head-to-head matchups, including a one-sided 6-4 6-0 victory in their round-robin match on Monday, but Svitolina has raised her level since.
"It's going to be another big challenge, of course, and I feel I have to do my homework," she said.
"But I feel I'm a completely different player from the first match. I was not playing the right way. I will give it my best shot."
Svitolina has now made the final all three times she has competed in the eight-player championships, winning it in 2018.
The $10 million tournament was moved from Riyadh to the Indian Wells Tennis Garden because of the US-Israeli war with Iran.

items.title: La Fed se encamina a subir las tasas en diciembre: el mercado ya anticipa otro aumento en enero
items.author: Enda Curran
items.summary: Los responsables de la Fed subieron las tasas un cuarto de punto en septiembre, hasta un rango objetivo del 3,75% al 4%, y luego las mantuvieron sin cambios en la reunión del FOMC celebrada en octubre ...
items.body: Bloomberg — El debate sobre la política monetaria de EE.UU. ya se ha trasladado a enero. En una serie de discursos y entrevistas esta semana, los funcionarios de la Reserva Federal consolidaron las expectativas del mercado respecto a una subida de las tasas de interés en diciembre y abrieron la posibilidad de los primeros aumentos consecutivos desde 2023. El martes cobró mayor urgencia la necesidad de aumentar las tasas de interés, cuando el informe de precios al consumidor de octubre mostró que la inflación se aceleró y se extendió a todos los bienes y servicios cotidianos. Ver más: ¿Qué señales de alerta deja el último dato de inflación de EE.UU. para la Fed? “La inflación es demasiado alta”, dijo el presidente de la Reserva Federal de Nueva York, John Williams, mientras que Austan Goolsbee, de la Reserva Federal de Chicago, describió los datos como “casi preocupantes”. La presidenta de la Reserva Federal de Dallas, Lorie Logan, dijo que los funcionarios podrían tener que subir las tasas “más rápidamente” de lo que esperaba, mientras que el gobernador de la Reserva Federal, Christopher Waller, llegó incluso a advertir que podría ser necesario un aumento de 50 puntos básicos el próximo mes. “Diciembre está claramente preparado para un alza de tasas de 25 puntos básicos”, afirmó Olu Sonola, jefe de economía estadounidense de Fitch Ratings. “Las verdaderas incógnitas son con qué rapidez se producirá la siguiente subida y cuántas más serán necesarias en última instancia”. Aproximadamente la mitad de los 19 miembros del Comité Federal de Mercado Abierto, y aproximadamente la mitad de quienes votarán en las reuniones de diciembre y enero, se han pronunciado a lo largo de la semana. En cuanto a las dos últimas cuestiones, las señales han sido contradictorias. Estas oscilaron desde la referencia de Waller a un aumento de gran envergadura hasta la reiteración por parte de Beth Hammack, de la Fed de Cleveland, de su preferencia por subidas más frecuentes y de menor magnitud, pasando por la postura de la presidenta de la Fed de Filadelfia, Anna Paulson, a favor de un ritmo gradual en los incrementos. Ver más: Citi prevé más alzas de tasas de la Fed, pero no espera un dólar más fuerte: las razones El viernes se conocieron más malas noticias cuando los datos revelaron que los precios al por mayor —que alimentan el indicador de inflación preferido por la Fed— subieron en octubre con respecto al año anterior a su ritmo más rápido desde 2022. Los costos de transporte y almacenamiento se dispararon, lo que se sumó a las pruebas de presiones persistentes sobre los precios en toda la economía. “Ahora parece que existe preocupación por adelantarse a la nueva aceleración, aumentar la frecuencia y, potencialmente, incrementar lo que el FOMC considera terminal”, es decir, hasta qué punto deberían subir las tasas de interés, dijo Michael Reid, jefe de economía estadounidense del Royal Bank of Canada. Los economistas de Bank of America ( BAC ) y de Santander US Capital Markets han aumentado el número de alzas que prevén tras la semana de datos y la avalancha de discursos. Bank of America prevé ahora subidas en las tres próximas reuniones de la Fed, mientras que Santander prevé dos aumentos, en diciembre y marzo. Los argumentos a favor de la cautela se basan en sectores de la economía vulnerables al aumento de los costos de financiación, como el mercado inmobiliario. Los datos económicos de esta semana pusieron de manifiesto lo deprimido que se encuentra ese sector, con las ventas de viviendas de segunda mano cayendo el mes pasado a su nivel más bajo en 16 años. La presidenta de la Fed de Boston, Susan Collins, reconoció el viernes que unas tasas de interés más altas pueden afectar a la asequibilidad de la vivienda, pero añadió que la estabilidad de los precios, a largo plazo, es más importante para el sector inmobiliario y para la economía en su conjunto. Ver más: Waller, de la Fed, abre la puerta a una posible subida de tasas de medio punto en diciembre “Me parece que la dirección adecuada para la política monetaria es clara”, dijo, refiriéndose a la necesidad de subir las tasas de interés. Sin embargo, en una entrevista con Bloomberg Television , no reveló cuál creía que sería el ritmo correcto. “No quiero adelantarme en cuanto a hasta dónde deberíamos llegar o a qué velocidad”, dijo. La volatilidad del mercado bursátil, vinculada a las preocupaciones sobre una desaceleración del auge de la inteligencia artificial, constituye otro motivo de inquietud. La gobernadora de la Reserva Federal, Michelle Bowman, advirtió de los riesgos, entre los que se incluye una fuerte caída de los precios de las acciones si la rentabilidad de las inversiones en IA no cumple con las expectativas. “La reducción de los precios de las acciones podría debilitar la capacidad de respuesta del gasto de los consumidores”, afirmó. “Y el aumento de las tasas de interés podría ejercer aún más presión sobre sectores de la economía sensibles a las fluctuaciones, como el sector inmobiliario y la inversión en pequeñas empresas”. Otra variable es la posibilidad de que los precios de la energía bajen en los próximos meses, lo que aliviaría la presión sobre los costos de los combustibles y supondría un respiro para los hogares y las empresas. El presidente de la Fed de Richmond, Tom Barkin, quien intervino el lunes, señaló que las tasas deben subir, pero a un ritmo prudente. “La mayoría de los funcionarios de la Reserva Federal parecen estar de acuerdo en la necesidad de subir las tasas de interés y en la preferencia por no precipitarse”, afirmó Eric Wallerstein, jefe de estrategia macroeconómica de Clocktower Group y anteriormente asesor del exgobernador de la Reserva Federal, Stephen Miran. Los responsables de la Fed subieron las tasas un cuarto de punto en septiembre, hasta un rango objetivo del 3,75% al 4%, y luego las mantuvieron sin cambios en la última reunión del FOMC celebrada en octubre. Ver más: Daly, de la Fed, dice que probablemente se necesiten más alzas de tasas para contener los precios El presidente de la Fed, Kevin Warsh, que no se ha pronunciado públicamente desde su rueda de prensa de octubre, tiene previsto hablar sobre su grupo de trabajo sobre inteligencia artificial y productividad en un acto que se celebrará el lunes. Pocos esperan que se desvíe de su preferencia declarada de no ofrecer ninguna orientación sobre las perspectivas a corto plazo de la política monetaria. Sin embargo, los inversores no están esperando y ya han descontado aumentos de un cuarto de punto para diciembre, enero y marzo. Antes de esta semana, los inversores habían anticipado incrementos en diciembre y marzo. Como ejemplo de la sacudida que supuso para los mercados la comunicación de la Fed de esta semana, los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro se dispararon tras las declaraciones de Waller y Logan, quienes intervinieron antes y después de que se publicaran el martes los datos de inflación, más elevados de lo esperado. El rendimiento de los bonos a dos años subió 19 puntos básicos hasta el 4,75% ese mismo día, su mayor alza desde que los anuncios arancelarios del presidente Donald Trump agitaran los mercados mundiales en abril de 2025. “Las directrices de la Reserva Federal son un tanto confusas y han provocado grandes fluctuaciones en los rendimientos de los bonos del Tesoro, y una vez más, dado que el presidente Warsh se abstiene de hacer comentarios, otros están llenando el vacío”, dijo la economista jefe de Nationwide, Kathy Bostjancic. En última instancia, la aceleración del crecimiento económico podría servir de pretexto a la Fed para subir las tasas. Los datos de la semana pasada mostraron que el empleo creció con fuerza en octubre y que la tasa de desempleo descendió ligeramente. Los responsables recibirán un informe más sobre el empleo y otra lectura de la inflación de octubre antes de reunirse de nuevo en diciembre. Pocos observadores esperan que ese conjunto de datos revele una desaceleración significativa. “El gradualismo es un error de política económica en una economía con fuerte crecimiento y alta inflación”, afirmó Robert Sockin, economista jefe para Estados Unidos de PGIM. “La historia sugiere que existe un alto riesgo de que este enfoque, en última instancia, lleve a un banco central a tener que endurecer su política monetaria más rápidamente y en mayor medida de lo que habría tenido que hacerlo de otro modo”. items.title: La tecnología del siglo XIX que Nvidia quiere cambiar para impulsar los centros de datos de IA
items.author: Emily Forgash, Michelle Ma, Mark Chediak
items.summary: La influencia de Nvidia ha impulsado una carrera para fabricar nuevos transformadores de potencia que sean más eficientes, que puedan gestionar mejor las amplias fluctuaciones de la demanda de centros ...
items.body: Bloomberg — La expansión de los centros de datos que sustentan la inteligencia artificial depende de un equipo cuya tecnología apenas ha evolucionado desde el siglo XIX. Sin embargo, eso podría estar a punto de cambiar. La influencia del gigante de los chips Nvidia Corp. ( NVDA ) ha impulsado una carrera para fabricar nuevos transformadores de potencia que sean más eficientes, que puedan gestionar mejor las amplias fluctuaciones de la demanda de los centros de datos y, lo que es fundamental, que ahorren espacio en las instalaciones para la capacidad de procesamiento. Ver más: Polémica de Jensen Huang opaca anuncio de alianzas de Nvidia con empresas de IA de Corea del Sur Para el empresario del sector de la energía solar Meir Adest, el plan de Nvidia supuso un momento de inspiración. Vio un mercado viable para un novedoso dispositivo eléctrico que su empresa, SolarEdge Technologies Inc., había comenzado a desarrollar en su momento, pero que abandonó durante una recesión del mercado. “Ya llevábamos años perfeccionando” una tecnología que eliminaría la necesidad de los transformadores tradicionales, afirmó Adest, cofundador de SolarEdge, en una entrevista. “Parecía el paso lógico” modificar sus prototipos para adaptarlos a la visión de Nvidia. El auge de los centros de datos está generando un gasto de capital de billones de dólares, y la prisa por ponerlos en funcionamiento se ve limitada sobre todo por el acceso a la red eléctrica. Las empresas de suministro eléctrico tienen dificultades para conectar las instalaciones previstas, lo que está provocando un aumento fuerte de los precios en algunas zonas de EE.UU. y generando una intensa reacción negativa, lo que, en parte, ha impulsado la victoria arrolladora de los demócratas en las elecciones de mitad de legislatura. Los demócratas victoriosos en una amplia franja de estados han prometido poner freno a la expansión de los centros de datos, especialmente en Texas, donde se está construyendo más de una cuarta parte de los centros de datos de EE.UU. Esto significa que la eficiencia energética y el aprovechamiento máximo de la infraestructura ya autorizada serán fundamentales para los constructores. Los nuevos dispositivos, conocidos como transformadores de estado sólido, ofrecen una solución para aliviar la presión sobre la red eléctrica —y podrían suponer una lucrativa oportunidad para las empresas que sean las primeras en comercializarlos. Ver más: ¿Qué negocios y conexiones en China tiene Alice Huang, señalada en la polémica del CEO de Nvidia? Los transformadores convencionales, utilizados comercialmente por primera vez a finales del siglo XIX, emplean bobinas, magnetismo y metal para convertir los niveles de voltaje. Estos equipos reducen los altos voltajes que transportan las redes eléctricas a niveles que pueden utilizarse en las instalaciones, y viceversa. Debido a la enorme cantidad de energía que necesita un centro de datos, estos equipos pueden ocupar una parte considerable de sus instalaciones. El año pasado, Nvidia instó al sector de los centros de datos a plantearse el cambio a una fuente de alimentación de corriente continua en lugar de la corriente alterna que prevalece en la actualidad. Ahí es donde entran en juego los transformadores de estado sólido. Constituyen un intento de utilizar electrónica de potencia y semiconductores para suministrar energía de corriente continua a los racks informáticos, al tiempo que se eliminan las etapas de conversión de potencia, lo que en su conjunto limita la pérdida de energía. Aunque los transformadores de estado sólido ya se han utilizado para mejorar la recarga de vehículos eléctricos, esta tecnología se encuentra, en el mejor de los casos, a un año de su comercialización para los centros de datos de EE.UU. En primer lugar, deben ser capaces de gestionar tensiones mucho más elevadas, grandes variaciones en la demanda y cumplir con los estándares de fiabilidad que requieren los centros de datos. Además, su fabricación e instalación resultan más costosas que las de los transformadores tradicionales. No obstante, estos retos no han frenado el entusiasmo por lo que pronto podría convertirse en una infraestructura fundamental de los futuros centros de datos. Una vez que los transformadores de estado sólido estén disponibles comercialmente, los analistas de Jefferies, liderados por Julien Dumoulin-Smith, predicen que el mercado estadounidense alcanzará los US$4.300 millones anuales para 2030. Las empresas que desarrollan los nuevos transformadores apuestan por que los operadores de centros de datos recurrirán a esta tecnología a largo plazo, ya que les permitirá liberar más espacio para los procesadores informáticos de IA, al tiempo que reducen los costos de los equipos. BloombergNEF estima que el ahorro ascenderá a US$1,39 millones por cada megavatio de demanda eléctrica de los centros de datos. (Algunos centros de datos propuestos superan los 1.000 megavatios, lo que equivale a la capacidad de un reactor nuclear tradicional). Los transformadores de estado sólido “convierten lo que históricamente ha sido un equipo pasivo en una infraestructura controlable, lo cual, dada la dinámica y la presión a la que está sometida la red eléctrica, es realmente importante”, dijo Victoria Beasley, socia fundadora de Gigascale Capital y patrocinadora de la empresa emergente Heron Power Electronics Co. Ver más: ¿Quién es Alice Huang, la presunta espía de Jensen Huang, CEO de Nvidia? El grupo chino Envision Group anunció la semana pasada que había logrado la primera implantación comercial a nivel mundial de un sistema para centros de datos que utiliza un transformador de estado sólido en su campus de Ulanqab, y las empresas estadounidenses se apresuran a ponerse al día. Las empresas solares que cotizan en bolsa, Enphase Energy Inc. y SolarEdge, han detectado la oportunidad de aprovechar su experiencia en electrónica de potencia y tecnología de corriente continua ante la ralentización del crecimiento de las ventas de sistemas solares residenciales. SolarEdge afirma que está probando un prototipo, mientras que Enphase realizó con éxito una demostración de su propio dispositivo a finales de octubre. Ambas empresas esperan realizar pruebas piloto de sus dispositivos el próximo año y comenzar los envíos comerciales en 2028. El CEO de Enphase, Badri Kothandaraman, dijo en una conferencia telefónica sobre los resultados del tercer trimestre que los dispositivos tienen “el potencial de convertirse en un negocio de ingresos anuales de mil millones de dólares” para la compañía solo en el mercado de centros de datos. Raghu Belur, director de productos de Enphase, calificó los nuevos transformadores como una medida “obvia” para los centros de datos, ya que permitirían ahorrar en la compra de energía de la red. “Para un centro de datos de un gigavatio, si se logra una eficiencia un 5% mayor, eso representa un ahorro de US$30 millones solo en costos de energía”, afirmó durante una reciente presentación sobre el transformador de estado sólido de la compañía en una conferencia de IA en Santa Clara, California. GE Vernova Inc., uno de los mayores fabricantes mundiales de equipos eléctricos, tiene previsto probar un transformador de estado sólido de 5 megavatios con un cliente a finales de este año, según declaró en verano su CEO, Scott Strazik. No obstante, señaló que los primeros pedidos no llegarán antes de 2027. El lanzamiento dependerá de la rapidez con la que los centros de datos adopten la corriente continua, señaló. Las empresas emergentes también están realizando sus propios intentos para desarrollar esta tecnología. Dos de ellas están dirigidas por antiguos empleados de Tesla Inc. ( TSLA ): Heron Power anunció en agosto que se encontraba en la fase de preproducción, antes de que se esperen sus primeras unidades de producción en serie en la segunda mitad de 2027, mientras que Amperesand Pte. declaró ese mismo mes que había puesto en marcha una línea de producción. DG Matrix Inc. está más avanzada en su desarrollo, con proyecciones de enviar hasta 2.000 transformadores en 2027, según declaró su CEO, Haroon Inam, en una entrevista. Axios informó el mes pasado que la compañía planea recaudar US$250 millones en una ronda de financiación Serie B el próximo año. DG Matrix ha pasado del sector de la carga de vehículos eléctricos, que requiere voltajes más bajos, al desarrollo de tecnología para centros de datos. Inam explicó que la tecnología de su empresa incluye múltiples “puertos” que permiten varias entradas y salidas de electricidad simultáneamente. Ver más: Acciones de Nvidia caen tras investigación de la junta directiva a su CEO, Jensen Huang, por una infidelidad Dumoulin-Smith predice que la dependencia de estas empresas de la nueva tecnología para generar ingresos variará según su tamaño. Para GE Vernova, se espera que los transformadores de estado sólido representen una parte mínima de sus ingresos, mientras que para Enphase y SolarEdge, estos dispositivos podrían alcanzar el 15% y el 11% de los ingresos de la compañía para 2030, respectivamente. Para validar sus proyectos a corto plazo, las empresas de energía solar deberán anunciar un programa piloto con un proveedor de servicios en la nube de gran tamaño, afirmó. Brian Dow, CEO de Ampersand, cree que, con el tiempo, una sola empresa acaparará entre el 30% y el 40% del mercado, y el sector, cada vez más saturado, irá eliminando a los pocos ganadores. Ninguna de estas innovaciones se estaría produciendo a tan gran escala sin el atractivo de las grandes empresas tecnológicas y su enorme poder adquisitivo, afirmó Caitilín McManus, analista de BNEF. “Ahora, con el capital adicional disponible gracias a los centros de datos, se está dando un impulso aún mayor”. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

SpaceX Starship returns to landing pad from orbit, acing test for reusable rockets

SpaceX's mega rocket Starship successfully returns to its launch pad and is caught by the launch tower following a test flight from Starbase, Texas, Saturday, Nov 14, 2026. (AP Photo/Eric Gay)

FAST

STARBASE, Texas: SpaceX's Starship spacecraft on Saturday (Nov 14) returned from a 22-hour voyage in orbit and descended for the first time into the grasp of giant mechanical arms at the Texas tower it was launched from a day earlier, a catch that is essential to the company's decade-long effort to develop a fully reusable rocket.
The 52m Starship fell out of thick clouds over SpaceX's Starbase launch site, reignited engines to flip itself vertical and slowly descended into the tower's "Mechazilla" arms, engines still roaring. Charred from the blazing heat of its return from space, the ship shut down its engines and hung still after the rocket system's longest mission yet.
"That was the missing link, the holy grail of spaceflight," SpaceX mission commentator Dan Huot said of the ship catch.
The towering two-stage rocket's Super Heavy booster - the rocket's bottom half - carried Starship to space on Friday, lifting off from SpaceX's Starbase, Texas, facilities. That booster had failed to make a similar return to the launch pad some 10 minutes after liftoff, nixing SpaceX's plan to recover both parts of the rocket for the first time.

But the Starship upper stage's successful return after orbiting Earth 14 times for 22.5 hours marked a key engineering milestone in the whirlwind, multibillion-dollar development of Starship, which billionaire Elon Musk sees as the future workhorse for SpaceX's lucrative Starlink satellite business, as well as ambitions to put data centres in orbit, return humans to the moon and, eventually, settle on Mars.

After deploying 26 Starlink satellites in orbit Friday night while cruising some 260km in altitude, Starship on Saturday fired one of its engines to begin an atmospheric plunge while flying eastward over the Pacific Ocean.
It faced blistering heat as its orbital speed of some 17,000 miles per hour slowed to a supersonic free-fall in the skies above SpaceX's Starbase facilities on the Gulf Coast of south Texas.
With its aerodynamic fins folded back, two small fittings near the top of Starship hooked onto the launch tower's mechanical arms that had closed in to grasp it, allowing the vessel to hang a few hundred feet off the ground.
Musk and SpaceX engineers began inspecting the ship within hours of its catch.
"Ship 42 looks great!" Musk wrote on X, posting photos and videos from the launch tower.
SHIP'S RETURN ADVANCES ROCKET REUSABILITY SpaceX's dominance in the global launch industry is centred on its workhorse Falcon 9 rocket, which has launched over 700 times since 2010. That rocket's first stage is reusable, but its second stage - the part that delivers payloads into orbit - is discarded into the ocean after each flight.
With Starship, Musk wants a rocket system that can fly to space and back in a manner and tempo akin to commercial airplanes, with minimal refurbishment between flights.

SpaceX's mega rocket Starship returns to its launch pad to be caught by the launch tower following a test flight from Starbase, Texas, on Nov 14, 2026. (Photo: AP/Eric Gay)

Though Saturday's Starship recovery is a key milestone in that effort, SpaceX has yet to recover both Starship stages in a single mission, which would mark the first-ever return of an orbital launch system.
And Starship's heat shield, composed of hundreds of black hexagonal tiles that protect it from the blazing heat of atmospheric reentry, is itself not yet fully reusable.
SpaceX is trying to engineer new tile designs that will require little to no refurbishment after each mission.
NASA's Space Shuttle system that ferried astronauts to the International Space Station before its 2011 retirement was partially reusable; its external fuel tanks that got it off Earth were discarded after each flight. The reusable spacecraft itself had to go through extensive refurbishment before re-flying.
SpaceX has spent more than US$15 billion on Starship's development. NASA has provided US$3.2 billion as part of a contract valued at more than US$4 billion that SpaceX won in 2021 to return humans to the moon using Starship under the space agency's Artemis program.
NASA expects Starship, along with another moon lander under development by Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin, to start crewed flights to the moon in 2028, though several challenging development milestones remain with both mooncraft.
For Starship, those milestones include demonstrating complex fuel transfers between Starship tanker rockets in orbit, a critical process that will enable the ship to travel beyond Earth's orbit to the moon.

Source: Reuters/rj/ec

But the Starship upper stage's successful return after orbiting Earth 14 times for 22.5 hours marked a key engineering milestone in the whirlwind, multibillion-dollar development of Starship, which billionaire Elon Musk sees as the future workhorse for SpaceX's lucrative Starlink satellite business, as well as ambitions to put data centres in orbit, return humans to the moon and, eventually, settle on Mars.

After deploying 26 Starlink satellites in orbit Friday night while cruising some 260km in altitude, Starship on Saturday fired one of its engines to begin an atmospheric plunge while flying eastward over the Pacific Ocean.
It faced blistering heat as its orbital speed of some 17,000 miles per hour slowed to a supersonic free-fall in the skies above SpaceX's Starbase facilities on the Gulf Coast of south Texas.
With its aerodynamic fins folded back, two small fittings near the top of Starship hooked onto the launch tower's mechanical arms that had closed in to grasp it, allowing the vessel to hang a few hundred feet off the ground.
Musk and SpaceX engineers began inspecting the ship within hours of its catch.
"Ship 42 looks great!" Musk wrote on X, posting photos and videos from the launch tower.
SHIP'S RETURN ADVANCES ROCKET REUSABILITY SpaceX's dominance in the global launch industry is centred on its workhorse Falcon 9 rocket, which has launched over 700 times since 2010. That rocket's first stage is reusable, but its second stage - the part that delivers payloads into orbit - is discarded into the ocean after each flight.
With Starship, Musk wants a rocket system that can fly to space and back in a manner and tempo akin to commercial airplanes, with minimal refurbishment between flights.

SpaceX's mega rocket Starship returns to its launch pad to be caught by the launch tower following a test flight from Starbase, Texas, on Nov 14, 2026. (Photo: AP/Eric Gay)

Though Saturday's Starship recovery is a key milestone in that effort, SpaceX has yet to recover both Starship stages in a single mission, which would mark the first-ever return of an orbital launch system.
And Starship's heat shield, composed of hundreds of black hexagonal tiles that protect it from the blazing heat of atmospheric reentry, is itself not yet fully reusable.
SpaceX is trying to engineer new tile designs that will require little to no refurbishment after each mission.
NASA's Space Shuttle system that ferried astronauts to the International Space Station before its 2011 retirement was partially reusable; its external fuel tanks that got it off Earth were discarded after each flight. The reusable spacecraft itself had to go through extensive refurbishment before re-flying.
SpaceX has spent more than US$15 billion on Starship's development. NASA has provided US$3.2 billion as part of a contract valued at more than US$4 billion that SpaceX won in 2021 to return humans to the moon using Starship under the space agency's Artemis program.
NASA expects Starship, along with another moon lander under development by Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin, to start crewed flights to the moon in 2028, though several challenging development milestones remain with both mooncraft.
For Starship, those milestones include demonstrating complex fuel transfers between Starship tanker rockets in orbit, a critical process that will enable the ship to travel beyond Earth's orbit to the moon.

Fed's Collins says gradual rate hikes best to manage economic risks

A number of Fed officials have said a more measured pace of rate increases allows the economy time to adjust to the rise in borrowing costs.

BOSTON: Fed eral Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins said on Saturday (Nov 14) she supported a steady pace of modest interest rate increases because that path of action better managed economic uncertainties.
When it comes to moving monetary policy to a tighter footing, "a steady, gradual path seems appropriate to me at the moment. But I'm open-minded," Collins told reporters at a conference held by her bank on housing issues in Boston.
“I do see the risks as two-sided on the real side of the economy," Collins said, with inflation high and its gains broadening throughout the economy, while the job market was stable with the potential to accelerate.
At the same time, there are the ongoing risks of more shocks hitting the economy, Collins said. Furthermore, “it's possible that the rise in medium to longer term rates that we've seen since the beginning of the year may actually weigh on demand more than I'm thinking,” and serve as another source of restraint on economic activity, she said.

For now, all of that argues against the Fed shifting to a more aggressive pace of rate rises to contain inflation that has overshot the Fed ’s 2 per cent target for more than five years, Collins said.

Related:

US yields climb, stocks fall as inflation data boosts chances for larger Fed rate hike

RATE INCREASES IN DECEMBER, JANUARY SEEN The Fed last raised rates in September, and it is widely expected to lift its current 3.75 per cent to 4 per cent interest rate target range by a quarter percentage point at the December 8-9 monetary policy meeting, following that with another increase in January.
Most Fed officials have signalled support for steady and small increases to help lower inflation, but last week's price data and the comments of Fed Governor Christopher Waller have suggested some on the Fed may want a bigger increase next month.
A number of Fed officials have said a more measured pace of rate increases allows the economy time to adjust to the rise in borrowing costs.
Collins cautioned that her expectation that the Fed can move gradually "doesn't necessarily mean a particular cadence." She also reiterated that the data flow from recent months has shifted where the Fed could end up in its current tightening cycle.
“I do think that the price data we've seen over the past three months, and the labor market on a stronger footing, does make me think that the path of policy rates over the, you know, next year might be a bit higher than I had thought a couple of months ago,” Collins said.

Source: Reuters/fs

KYIV: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy escalated his criticism of SpaceX on Saturday (Nov 14), saying speed restrictions on its military-grade Starshield satellite terminals had dangerous political implications and undermined critical air defences.
Zelenskyy said Starshield terminals operating in temporarily Russian-occupied territories of Ukraine had been limited to a maximum speed of 161 kph for the past five days, hampering Ukraine's military capabilities.
The Ukrainian Defence Ministry has raised the issue with SpaceX at the institutional level, Zelenskyy said.
"The restrictions have now been in place for five days. They say it is some kind of technical issue. We do not believe that is the case," Zelenskyy told reporters in remarks released by his office on Saturday.

"If you impose restrictions there, you are already partially recognising the temporarily occupied territories as not ours. And that is why I believe we have the right to raise this issue and restore the speed – so that there are no restrictions at all."
Zelenskyy said the speed restrictions made it more difficult for Ukrainian air defence units to intercept Russian jet-powered drones and made Ukrainian cities more vulnerable. He said he had ordered his top military and foreign ministry officials to address the issue and seek clarification.
SpaceX has pushed back against the allegations, denying that it introduced new restrictions or made any changes to its satellite operations.
It is the second such outage in recent weeks. In mid-October, Ukrainian officials said that SpaceX limited the speed of Starlink and its Starshield communication systems to about 160 kph amid tensions with US President Donald Trump's administration over Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries. Service was then restored on Oct 24.

WASHINGTON: US air travel is not expected to return to normal schedules until late on Sunday (Nov 15), the head of the FAA said, as the aviation system gradually recovers from a nationwide flight shutdown that officials blamed on routine maintenance gone awry.
As of 9.35pm ET, airlines on Saturday had cancelled more than 6,400 US flights and delayed more than 8,000, according to FlightAware, an aviation website. That followed about 9,200 flights cancelled and 7,500 delayed on Friday after the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop because of disruptions to air traffic communications. FlightAware said 875 flights scheduled for Sunday were already cancelled.
Federal Aviation Administration head Bryan Bedford said on Saturday that he expected airline operations to largely return to normal by late Sunday. He also apologised for the disruption, adding that the system remains stable.
The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday that halted nearly all departing flights for almost five hours. It was the longest nationwide halt to air travel since the attacks of Sep 11, 2001, and one of the single worst US travel days ever.

The issue prompted the White House to convene an emergency meeting in the Situation Room on Friday and federal agencies to scramble to determine if it was a cyberattack. But the problem was traced to FAA contractor L3Harris' installation of at least one new router at a remote facility, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on Saturday.
"We're working to determine whether we had incompetence, meaning was it user error or installer error from L3Harris, or did they install a faulty router? We haven't determined what the fault was," Duffy said at a press conference.
The Professional Aviation Safety Specialists, a union representing FAA safety employees, said the issue was isolated to two routers that were updated Friday. An official told Reuters it was believed the routers were in Arkansas and Texas.
An FAA official said the agency conducted a safety assessment before the work. The union said PASS-represented technicians were not involved in the upgrades that led to the ground stop.
L3Harris said it took the issue seriously and is supporting the FAA in its investigation. Its shares last traded down about 4% after hours on Friday.

Related:

US FAA says it will phase out floppy disks from air traffic control by 2028

US FAA says Boeing 737 MAX software glitch poses no safety issue

FAA begins use of AI tool in bid to reduce flight delays

OVERLOADED COMMUNICATIONS CENTRES Duffy said the trouble began on Friday afternoon, when air traffic control centres experienced instability in radar and communications systems. The router issue led to data overloading other communications centres, officials said.
"We had over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, and what that did was (it) gave us issues with our communication with airplanes, and it also caused some disruption with our radar," Duffy added.
The issue affected communications at 17 of the FAA's 22 en route centres, which control aircraft during the cruise portion of a flight. Bedford said the FAA ordered the ground stop in case a centre lost all communications. "No facilities went dark. Nothing was fully lost," Bedford added.
The FAA said it was doing additional testing with L3Harris to see if there are any additional risks.
Delta Air Lines, United Airlines and American Airlines all cancelled about 25 per cent of their flights on Saturday, while JetBlue cancelled nearly 45 per cent. Airlines have issued travel waivers allowing passengers to rebook flights for later dates without cost.
Though the FAA lifted the ground stop on Friday evening, the disruption for passengers was far from over, with tens of thousands of people stranded in airports. Airlines were trying to get flight crews and other personnel in position to resume flights.
The disruption stranded some college football teams on Friday before games scheduled for Saturday.

United States Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy takes questions as US Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin looks on in the James S Brady Press Briefing Room at the White House in Washington DC, Nov 13 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Elizabeth Frantz)

FUNDS SOUGHT TO FIX SYSTEM STRAIN Friday's disruption is the latest and most dramatic sign of strain on a US air traffic control system beset by ageing technology, equipment and communications problems and a shortage of several thousand controllers.
Duffy called on Friday for US$50 billion in funding to upgrade air traffic control systems, up from his earlier request of US$30 billion - after Congress approved US$12.5 billion last year.
House Speaker Mike Johnson told Fox News on Saturday that he supports approving more funding for air traffic this year. Johnson's Republicans control Congress until next year, when Democrats will take over because of their gains in the November 3 midterm elections.
US Representatives Rick Larsen and Andre Carson, Democrats slated next year to chair the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and aviation subcommittee, respectively, said in a joint statement Saturday that their panels will "hold the administration accountable for what happened to make sure this chaos does not happen again."
Since receiving US$12.5 billion last year, the Transportation Department has awarded contracts worth US$4.3 billion but only spent US$1 billion, Larsen and Carson said.

Source: Reuters/fs/rj/ec

items.title: New to The Street Show #780 Premieres Tonight on Bloomberg Television with Robo.ai, American Fusion, Stewards Investment Capital and FreeCast
items.summary: Jane King hosts conversations on sovereign AI, fusion energy, global private credit and partner-led streaming infrastructure, airing at 6:30 p.m. ET across the United States, Latin America, MENA and ...
items.body:
News
/ ACCESS Newswire
/ New to The Street Show #780 Premieres Tonight on Bloomberg Television with Robo.ai, American Fusion, Stewards Investment Capital and Fr…

New to The Street Show #780 Premieres Tonight on Bloomberg Television with Robo.ai, American Fusion, Stewards Investment Capital and FreeCast 7 min read

AIIO AMFN CAST SWRD
Jane King hosts conversations on sovereign AI, fusion energy, global private credit and partner-led streaming infrastructure, airing at 6:30 p.m. ET across the United States, Latin America, MENA and Southeast Asia
NEW YORK CITY, NY / ACCESS Newswire / November 14, 2026 / AI is driving record spending on data centers, and with it, soaring costs for storage, bandwidth and power. Fusion developers are racing to deliver clean, around-the-clock energy. International investors are looking for returns that don't move with the rest of their portfolios. And companies that already own the customer relationship want to own the screen, too.
Tonight, New to The Street brings leaders working on each of those challenges to a global business audience as Show #780 premieres at 6:30 p.m. ET on Bloomberg Television as sponsored programming, with distribution across the United States, Latin America, the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) and Southeast Asia.
Hosted by Jane King, Show #780 features executive conversations with:
Ralf R. Debbas , President of Robo.ai Inc. AIIO
Dr. Jasem Al Mansoori , Chief Executive Officer of ALIF Holding
Mansoor Ali Khan , Chief Technology Officer of Neurovia AI
Brent Nelson , Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of American Fusion Inc. AMFN
Bilal Adam , Chief Executive Officer of Stewards Investment Capital
William "Bill" Mobley , Founder and Chief Executive Officer of FreeCast, Inc. CAST
"Show #780 is about the infrastructure behind the next economy," said Vince Caruso, Co-Founder and CEO of New to The Street. "A UAE-based, Nasdaq-listed group building sovereign AI and industrial capability. A fusion company opening its technology to independent review. An investment firm connecting emerging and developed markets. And a software company turning every internet connection into a media business. These are the stories our audience in every region tunes in for. No politics. No current events. Only Opportunities To Consider™."
INSIDE SHOW #780
Robo.ai Inc. AIIO : Where Global AI Investment Meets Local Capability
In a three-executive panel, Jane King asks where Robo.ai fits in the AI investment cycle. Ralf R. Debbas, President of Robo.ai, describes the company as a UAE-based, Nasdaq-listed group "connecting regional technology with global market reach."
He outlines its main operating businesses: Neurovia AI, focused on visual data efficiency; ALIF Holding, which brings industrial integration, manufacturing and execution; and Quantum Core Capital (QC Capital), which contributes operating revenue and is developing AI applications including AI-generated video and content creation.
"Our ambition is to help build sovereign AI capabilities within the UAE itself and the wider region," Debbas said, "technology that can be deployed, supported and developed locally."
Dr. Jasem Al Mansoori, Chief Executive Officer of ALIF Holding, Robo.ai's Abu Dhabi-based industrial group, draws on more than 30 years at the UAE Ministry of Interior. "This experience taught me the importance of reliable solutions and strong local support," he said. ALIF is developing an industrial base in the UAE for engineering and manufacturing, and aims to use AI to help industrial customers work more efficiently and make better decisions.
Mansoor Ali Khan, Chief Technology Officer of Neurovia AI, explains why efficiency matters as AI computing competition intensifies and memory and storage costs rise. Khan notes that the large majority of the world's data is visual and unstructured.
Neurovia's flagship NeuroStream™ platform is designed to reduce the volume of visual data that is transmitted, processed and stored. In a company demonstration shown on air, a 12.15 GB 4K video file was reduced to 421 MB, a reduction of more than 96%. Khan said the goal is to address the main costs of AI (storage, compute, transmission and power) and make AI "more affordable and sustainable." Actual results depend on deployment conditions and use-case validation.
Learn more at roboai.group.
American Fusion Inc. AMFN : Independent Review, a New Texas Campus and a Busy Six Months
Chairman and CEO Brent Nelson returns to update Jane King on American Fusion's Texatron™ aneutronic fusion engine. Nelson says an independent third-party reviewer recently completed an on-site evaluation of the technology, with a final report expected later this month. "The draft highlights look good so far," he said, adding that the company hopes the report will confirm "that we're on the right track."
Nelson, who added the CEO title in late October, says his priorities for the next six months include closing on the company's North Texas "Ranch" facility, which American Fusion expects by Thanksgiving, and developing the property. The company is also moving from its temporary facility into new lab and office space, and plans to build its own testing bunker at the Ranch. "We're still operating and testing the Texatron on a daily basis," Nelson said, "and our data is getting better."
He also says the company's patent program remains active, with new applications being written daily, and that its data center proposals are moving forward.
Learn more at americanfusionenergy.com.
Stewards Investment Capital CEO Bilal Adam on Global Investing, Private Credit and Financial Inclusion
Bilal Adam, Chief Executive Officer of Stewards Investment Capital, joins Jane King to discuss the firm's international investment approach, private credit solutions and commitment to financial inclusion. A chartered accountant from South Africa with a background in investment banking, Adam describes building a business with activities spanning South Africa, Mauritius, the United States and Monaco.
Adam discusses the firm's investment philosophy, which he says starts with "aiming to do good first," and its relationship with Nasdaq-listed Stewards, Inc. SWRD , a U.S.-based diversified financial platform led by President and CEO Shaun Quin, which provides financing to small businesses across the United States. Stewards Investment Capital is affiliated with, but separate from, Stewards, Inc. He also highlights telecommunications tower investments aimed at expanding connectivity and financial inclusion in rural African communities.
The conversation explores how Stewards Investment Capital provides pension funds, institutions, family offices and high-net-worth investors with access to private credit, portfolio diversification and international investment opportunities, including a private credit approach that funds fractional amounts of loans to small businesses.
Learn more at stewardsinvestment.com.
FreeCast, Inc. CAST : "The Connection Is Just the Beginning"
Founder and CEO William Mobley explains why FreeCast is "not another streaming service." Instead, the company provides the software infrastructure that lets telecom companies, wireless carriers, internet providers, satellite companies and membership organizations launch their own branded entertainment hubs, offering free television, premium subscriptions, sports, advertising and commerce. "They bring the customers," Mobley said. "We bring the media and monetization technology."
Mobley walks through PEAC, FreeCast's metric for "partner-enabled addressable customers," which measures potential distribution reach through enterprise agreements. He is clear that PEAC does not represent active users, paying subscribers or confirmed revenue. He describes the company's job as converting that reach into activated users, transactions and, ultimately, revenue across advertising, subscriptions, pay-per-view, live sports, rentals and commerce.
"We don't need Netflix to lose for FreeCast to succeed," Mobley said. "We want more content and more services participating in our marketplaces."
Learn more at freecast.com.
FEATURED COMMERCIALS
SafeSpace Global Corporation SSGC : An AI-powered safety and security platform designed to help protect the vulnerable in schools, senior care, addiction treatment, correctional facilities and houses of worship. "Smarter technology, faster response, safer spaces."
T-REX Acquisition Corp. TRXA : Completed a strategic refinancing of its Orofino, Idaho data center and added a new appointment to its board of directors.
Big Sky Industrial BSIN : Advancing helium production, carbon management and strategic energy infrastructure through its flagship Big Sky Carbon Hub, targeting demand from AI, semiconductors, healthcare and aerospace.
Acurx Pharmaceuticals, Inc. ACXP : Developing what could be the first new class of antibiotics in nearly 40 years, with the FDA agreeing to consider a future application for lead drug ibezapolstat based on two planned trials, Pathfinder and Aspire.
HOW TO WATCH
Bloomberg Television: Tonight, Saturday, November 14, 2026, at 6:30 p.m. ET, with distribution across the United States, Latin America, MENA and Southeast Asia
New to The Street TV on YouTube (5.44M+ subscribers): https://www.youtube.com/@NewtoTheStreetTV
NewsOut on YouTube (1.24M+ subscribers): https://www.youtube.com/@NewsOutChannel
Following the broadcast, every segment will be distributed across the New to The Street TV and NewsOut YouTube channels, which together have more than 6.6 million subscribers.
MEET THE COMPANIES 2027: NEW YORK, ATLANTIC CITY AND LAS VEGAS
New to The Street's Meet The Companies tour brings presenting companies face to face with family offices, accredited investors and high-net-worth individuals in three cities in 2027. Every presentation is filmed and distributed across New to The Street's U.S., Latin America, MENA and Southeast Asia platforms and its 6.6M+ subscriber YouTube network, so each company reaches a guaranteed audience well beyond the room. No vendor pitches.
New York - Thursday, January 7, 2027: The Hudson Yards Penthouse, 455 Tenth Avenue PH, New York, NY 10018, the week before the Needham Growth Conference, with a cocktail reception on Wednesday, January 6
Atlantic City - Thursday, January 28, 2027
Las Vegas - June 17-18, 2027
Each event hosts up to 20 presenting companies, with 20-minute slots that include a 15-minute presentation and Q&A. For Atlantic City and Las Vegas presenters, New to The Street pays for your stay.
Confirmed New York Presenters
Glint (glintpay.com)
TMC the metals company Inc. TMC
American Fusion Inc. AMFN
Big Sky Industrial BSIN
T-REX Acquisition Corp. TRXA
Stewards, Inc. SWRD
Roadzen Inc. RDZN
Smile Design Manhattan
Additional presenters will be announced. Accredited investors only. Apply to attend: John@NewtoTheStreet.com. Companies interested in a presenting slot can contact John Battenfield at John@NewtoTheStreet.com.
ABOUT NEW TO THE STREET
Founded in 2009, New to The Street is a sponsored and syndicated business television platform serving public companies, emerging-growth businesses and companies preparing to enter the public markets. Co-founded and led by CEO Vince Caruso, New to The Street combines weekly Bloomberg Television broadcasts across the United States, Latin America, MENA and Southeast Asia with long-form executive interviews, television commercials, earned media, social-media distribution, NewsOut video press-release coverage, accredited-investor events and premium outdoor advertising, including Times Square billboards. The platform has worked with more than 200 public companies. No politics. No current events. Only Opportunities To Consider™.
